text.zh:
仪式很少随便发生。
它通常会创造一个特殊空间：
把普通空间变成特殊空间。
一套“动作”——人到底要做什么
这是仪式最容易被看见的部分。
这些动作往往有一个特点：
它们本身并不一定具有现实效率。
比如对着神像鞠躬，并不会直接改变天气。
但这个动作在仪式里面具有意义。
所以仪式动作可以理解成一种“象征性的语言”。
你现在要从日常状态进入另外一种状态。
节日 → 普通的一天变成“值得共同记忆的一天”
所以仪式其实是在制造一种状态转换
text.en:
The rituals rarely happen at random.
It usually creates a special space:
Turning ordinary space into special space.
A set of actions -- what do people do?
This is the most visible part of the ritual.
These actions often have one feature:
They themselves are not necessarily realistic and efficient.
For example, bowing to the statue does not change the weather directly.
But this move has meaning in the ceremony.
So the ritual moves can be understood as a “symbol language”.
You're going from routine to another state.
Days, days, days, days.
So the ceremony is actually creating a state conversion.

Looking at Asia, it is more common for people living in cities to eat breakfast outside, and Japan's preferential breakfast with the cultural identity of life shared by Asian urban societies [images].

text.zh:
宗教、仪式、市场：

能量石

将具有能量的物品带在身上，与佩戴传统护身符的行为相似。护身符不是单纯的物品，是在神佛面前进行祈福消灾的仪式后被赐予的灵物。人们相信护身符的能量是由宗教仪式赋予的。如此想来，看似与过去毫无关联的能量石中，也存在着与传统宗教民俗类似的地方。不过，能量石的普及受到了媒体与市场的巨大影响，而且由于对能量石的理解不同，出现了广泛的个体选择差异，这两点与传统宗教习俗还是有较大区别的。
text.en:
Religion, ceremony, market:

Energy Stone

Bringing energy-capable objects to your body is similar to wearing traditional amulets. The amulet is not a mere thing, but a spiritual thing that is given after a ritual of prayer and healing before the Buddha. People believe that the energy of the amulet is given by religious rituals. In this sense, there is a similarity to traditional religious folklore among energy stones that seem to have nothing to do with the past. However, the spread of energy stones has been greatly influenced by the media and the market, and a wide variety of individual choices has emerged as a result of different understandings of energy stones, which are still quite different from traditional religious practices.

text.zh:
所谓“俗”​，包含下述四重含义中的某一个，或是它们的任意组合。

这四重含义分别是：
(1)与支配性权力相左的事物；
(2)无法完全用启蒙主义之理性来解释的事物；
(3)与“普遍”​“主流”​“中心”的立场相悖的事物；
(4)与正式制度保持一定距离的事物。

description.zh: 《大家的民俗学》岛村恭则
description.en: "The Folklore of All"

text.zh: 那么，让我们总结一下，​“什么是民俗学”​。我认为，民俗学是采用了对抗18世纪以法国为中心的启蒙主义、19世纪初以统治欧洲为目标的拿破仑的霸权主义的形式，由德国的赫尔德、格林兄弟奠定基础，之后扩散到世界各地，在各自的区域有个性地发展的一门学问。民俗学内在性地理解与“作为霸权、普遍、主流、中心的社会位置”处于不同位置的人们的生活，包括厘清其与“作为霸权、普遍、主流、中心的社会位相”之间的关系。从而使以“作为霸权、普遍、主流、中心的社会位相”为基准而形成的知识体系相对化，并创造出超越这一知识体系的知识。
text.en: So let's just say, "What's folklore?" Folklore, I think, was in the form of a doctrine against the 18th century of French-centred enlightenmentism and Napoleon ' s hegemony at the beginning of the 19th century, aimed at European domination, laying the foundations of Germany ' s Held and Green Brothers, which then spread throughout the world and developed in a personal way in their respective regions. Folklore intrinsically understands the lives of people who are in different positions “as hegemonic, universal, mainstream, central social position”, including clarifying their relationship with “hegemonistic, universal, mainstream, central social status”. This leads to the relativization of knowledge systems based on “hegemonic, universal, mainstream, central social status” and to the creation of knowledge beyond that knowledge system.

description.zh: 那些相信自己处于“主流”​“中心”的位置，并把自己的逻辑作为“普世”价值强加给他人的势力，民俗学努力与之抗衡。《大家的民俗学》岛村恭则
description.en: Folklore struggles against those who believe that they are “mainstream” “centres” and impose their logic as “universal” values on others. "The Folklore of All"

description.zh: 《大家的民俗学》岛村恭则

text.zh:
民俗学是一门什么样的学问？接下来，让我们步入正题。

所谓民俗学，指的是从“俗”的观点来研究“民”​（人类、人们）的学问。我认为“俗”​，包含下述四重含义中的某一个，或是它们的任意组合。这四重含义分别是：
(1)与支配性权力相左的事物；
(2)无法完全用启蒙主义之理性来解释的事物；
(3)与“普遍”​“主流”​“中心”的立场相悖的事物；
(4)与正式制度保持一定距离的事物。而本书书名中的“vernacular”​，则是“俗”的英语表达。

text.zh:
在柳田国男的初期作品中，有一本题为《远野物语》的著作，于1910年（明治四十三年）出版发行。这本书收录了岩手县远野地区的各种不可思议的传说，而书的开头如此写道

愿广述其事，使平地人战栗。

这里的“其事”指的是岩手县远野地区的人们口口相传的故事，​“平地人”则指代在启蒙主义思想影响下迈向现代化的都市居民。这句话如果转换成现代文来说，是“希望通过讲述这些故事，让城里的人们不寒而栗”​。
text.en:
One of the first works by Yanada Kuoji was published in 1910 (forty-three years). This book contains incredible legends from the Faraway District of Iwaki County, and the beginning of the book says,

May the plains be shaken with a broad statement.

Here, the word “things” refers to the stories of the people in the far-off area of Iwataka County, and the “landlanders” refers to urban dwellers who are moving towards modernization under the influence of the enlightened ideology. The phrase, if translated into modern writing, is “I hope that by telling these stories people in the city will be shaken”.

text.zh:
从“folklore”到“vernacular”


vernacular？

在现代美国民俗学中，​“俗”被表述为“vernacular”一词。在以语言学为首的人文、社会科学体系里，​“vernacular”一词长期以来被用以指代与具有权威性、正统性的语言相对的“俗语”​。
text.en:
From "folklore" to "vernacular"


What is it, Vernacular?

In modern American folklore, the word “feed” is used as the word “vernacular”. The term “vernacular” has long been used in the humanist and social science system, headed by linguistics, to refer to “fiction” vis-à-vis authoritative and orthodox language.

description.zh: 《大家的民俗学》岛村恭则
description.en: "The Folklore of All"

text.zh:
民俗学诞生于18世纪的德国，哲学家、思想家约翰•哥特弗雷德•赫尔德(Johann Gottfried von Herder, 1744—1803)构建了这门学科的基础。

在当时的欧洲，以英国、法国为首的“启蒙主义”(the Enlightenment)思想，成为引领该时代的主流思想。所谓启蒙主义，指的是崇尚理性，试图消除一切非理性事物的思想。​“启蒙”的“蒙”​，是蒙昧无知的“蒙”​；​“启”是“开启”的“启”​，是“点亮”的意思，所以“启蒙”指的是，将处于非理性世界中的蒙昧无知的人们，引向光明的世界，开启其心智。启蒙主义思想不仅在其发源地英国、法国深入人心，还流传到了欧洲各地，德国等国家也受到了启蒙主义的巨大影响。但是，赫尔德却对这种思想不以为然。启蒙主义的理念是理性和“普世”性，即世界上的人们，不论他们身处何处，以何种生活方式生活着，对于大家来说，合乎理性的思考及思考的结果都应该是，且必须是普遍适用的。

因此，信奉启蒙主义的人们，否定自己所处社会的固有的生活方式、思维方式，以及日常使用的土著语言，认为这一切恰是应被“启蒙”的对象。

与之相对，赫尔德认为，不应盲目顺从源于法国的舶来思想，而应探求而应探求根植于自身生活的生存之道。

他主张重视、发掘德国本土的日常生活、语言及思想。本书中，我们姑且将赫尔德的这种思想，称为“反启蒙主义”​。基于这种想法，赫尔德开始收集民谣。


之所以选择民谣，是因为他觉得在人们日常生活中传唱的民谣里，栖息着“民众之魂”​。赫尔德不仅亲自编撰《民谣集》​，还号召更多的人加入到民谣的收集工作中来。继赫尔德之后登场的是格林兄弟，即雅各布•格林(Jacob Ludwig Karl Grimm, 1785—1863) 和威廉•格林(Wilhelm Karl Grimm，1786—1859)。


他们虽受赫尔德的影响，但与赫尔德的“民谣”不同，格林兄弟进行的是“故事”​（民间故事、传说、神话）的收集与研究。成果有《格林童话集：献给孩子和家庭的童话》​（也就是所谓的《格林童话集》​）​、​《德国传说集》等。从19世纪后半叶到20世纪初，赫尔德、格林兄弟所从事的研究（即民俗学研究）​，不仅影响了欧洲，还辐射到世界各地。在欧洲的芬兰、爱沙尼亚、拉脱维亚、立陶宛、挪威、瑞典、爱尔兰、苏格兰、威尔士、布列塔尼、瑞士、匈牙利、斯拉夫诸国、希腊等地，以及欧洲之外的美国、印度、日本、中国、韩国、俄罗斯、菲律宾、巴西、阿根廷、尼日利亚、加纳等国家，纷纷开始进行民俗学研究，并在各自的土地上孕育出独具特色的民俗学。时至今日，这些国家和地区的民俗学研究依然很兴盛。随着民俗学的普及，研究范围也得以拓展。除了民谣、故事外，研究对象涉及了人们生活的方方面面。
text.en:
Folklore was born in Germany in the 18th century. Johann Gottfried von Herder, 1744-1803, formed the basis of the subject.

In Europe at the time, the idea of “the Enlightenment”, led by Britain and France, became the dominant idea that led the era. Enlightenmentism refers to ideas that embrace reason and try to eliminate anything irrational. The “enlightenment” is the “enlightenment” of obscurity; the “initiation” is the “opening” of `opening', meaning `lighting', so the “initiation” refers to bringing the obscurant ignorance of people in an irrational world to light and opening their minds. Enlightenmentism is not only in Britain and France, where it originates, but also in all parts of Europe, and countries like Germany are greatly influenced by it. Held, however, is not convinced of this idea. The idea of enlightenmentism is rational and “universal”, that people in the world, wherever they may be, live in a way of life, and for all, the results of rational thinking and reflection should be and must be universal.

Thus, the people of Enlightenment reject the way of life inherent in the society in which they live, the way of thinking, and the indigenous languages that they use on a day-to-day basis, all of which should be the object of “initiation”.

By contrast, Helder believes that it is important not to follow the ideas of French origin blindly, but rather to explore ways of survival rooted in his own life.

He advocates the importance and discovery of everyday life, language and ideas in Germany itself. In this book, we speak of the idea of Held as “anti-enlightened”. On the basis of this idea, Held began to collect folk rumours.


He chose folklore because he felt that “the soul of the people” was found in folk rumours that people sing in their daily lives. Not only did Held personally compile the Rumours, he also called for more people to join the collection. He was followed by the Green brothers Jacob Ludwig Karl Grimm, 1785-1863 and William Karl Grimm, 1786-1859.


They were influenced by Held, but unlike Held, the Green brothers were engaged in the collection and study of “story” (civil stories, legends, myths). The results were the Green Story Book: A Story for Children and Families (the so-called Green Story Book), the German Story. From the second half of the 19th century to the beginning of the 20th century, the studies carried out by the Hilde and Green brothers (i.e. folklore studies) affected not only Europe but also the world. In Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Sweden, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, Brittany, Switzerland, Hungary, Slavs, Greece and other countries outside Europe, such as the United States, India, Japan, China, Korea, Russia, the Philippines, Brazil, Argentina, Nigeria, Ghana, among others, have embarked on folklore studies and have produced unique folklore on their lands. Folklore research in these countries and regions has continued to flourish today. With the popularization of folklore, the scope of research has also been expanded. In addition to folklore and stories, the subjects covered all aspects of people ' s lives.

text.zh:
俗？




任何一个集团，只要人们至少共有一种相同的要素，就可以用“folk”一词来描述它。该集团的凝结要素多种多样，可以是共同的职业，也可以是共同的语言或宗教。而这个集团共享的知识，就是folklore。（Alan Dundes: The Study of Folklore, Prentice Hall,1965年）如此定义之后，他补充说道，不仅是农民，煤炭矿工、铁路员工、棒球选手、冲浪运动员（冲浪人士）​、摩托车骑手、电脑程序员、办公室职员、医生、科学家等，也都有自己群体的folklore。在邓迪斯的倡导下，美国民俗学的研究对象得以拓展，各类事物均被视为folklore进行研究。

例如都市传说、被称为涂鸦的都市壁画、办公室职员共享的幽默、遭受犯罪伤害的纽约人的经历之谈、童子军的习惯和礼仪、急救队员们的经验谈、铁路劳动者的讲述、被称作“Outsider Art”的素人绘画、万圣节、狂欢节等。



花钱去一个工作坊是不是俗？



俗的实践？

动态的俗？
text.en:
Common?




In any group, the term “folk” could be used to describe it as long as there was at least one common element. The condensation elements of the group are diverse, ranging from a common occupation to a common language or religion. And the knowledge this group shares is the funklore. After such a definition, he added that not only farmers, coal miners, railway workers, baseball players, surfers (surfers), motorcyclists, computer programmers, office clerks, doctors, scientists, etc., also had their own group, volklore. At the initiative of Dundis, American folklore has been expanded to include all kinds of research that are considered to be funklore.

For example, urban legends, urban murals known as graffiti, humor shared by office staff, experiences of New Yorkers who had suffered from crime, boy scout habits and rituals, lessons learned by first responders, accounts of railway workers, sketches of a veritable called “Outsider Art”, Halloween, Carnival, etc.

A common practice?

今日剧目：制造麻烦

演出简介：

麻烦精和捣蛋鬼被台风吹着走了一个月，再次因为无墙艺术节来到了海口。麻烦精还沉浸在过家家的琐碎中，想着开学了是不是也应该收收心，牙齿紧紧握在口中；捣蛋鬼在漂流中遇到新朋友、又和老朋友相聚，但和他们一起聊天的诱惑实在太大了，也不想停下去厕所。

两人时常听到有人问小朋友“你要去一下厕所吗”？也时常问自己“我现在要不要趁机去一下厕所？” 东村新妇漂流中，也时常在找一个可以尿尿的地方。如果人类不需要去尿尿就好了！如果我暂时忘记怎么尿尿就好了。



这是关于麻烦精和捣蛋鬼讨厌害怕拔牙，忘记怎么尿尿，还有一路漂流的故事。

随机掉落一切麻烦事，捣蛋所有伤脑筋。

Presentation:

The troublemakers and troublemakers were blown away by the typhoon for a month and again came to the mouth for the Wallless Art Festival. The troublemaker is still in the care of his family, and he wonders if he should start school and hold his teeth in his mouth; the troublemakers meet new friends in the drift and meet old friends, but the temptation to talk to them is too great to stop going to the bathroom.

Two people often hear kids say, "Do you want to go to the bathroom?" And sometimes he asks himself, "Do I need to go to the bathroom now?" If only humans didn't have to pee! If only I forgot how to pee for a while.



It's a story about troublemakers and troublemakers who hate to be afraid to pull teeth, forget how to pee, and drift.

Randomly drops everything in trouble, screws all the brains.

text.zh:
# 项目 / 活动名称

**“我忘记怎么尿尿”：制作天使娃娃**

## 一、主题阐释

“过家家”是一种很小的游戏。

孩子们用几张纸、一块布、一把椅子，就可以假装这里是一个家；东村新妇也一直在“过家家”。

我们搭一个临时的台子，假装它是剧场；拿起一个木偶，假装它是演员；把一张床变成舞台，把旧布变成衣服，把生活里随手可见的东西变成戏剧。

一个孩子突然说：

> **“忘记怎么尿尿了**
> **？”**

它不是在问一个生理动作，而是在问：

**我的身体应该按照什么方式存在？**

因为从小我们就在学习一套关于身体的社会规则。

一个孩子从什么时候开始知道：

这是对的，那是错的；

这里可以去，那里不可以；

这个动作可以被看见，那个动作必须隐藏；

这个身体应该这样使用，那个身体应该那样使用。

而当我们暂时忘记这些规则的时候，会不会获得一次重新想象生活的机会？

“天使娃娃”因此成为一个很小的实验：

我们想和孩子们一起，把这个游戏继续下去。

**“天使娃娃”就是我们一起做出来的一个过家家玩具。**

我们邀请孩子先画一幅画。画可以是真实的，也可以完全来自想象。随后，我们一起用布料和针线缝制一个天使娃娃，把孩子的画缝进娃娃。

娃娃的肚子像一个小小的相框，里面装着孩子的画。

天使娃娃是最容易做的一个娃娃

它可以被抱起来，可以被带回家，也可以成为一个演员。

我们会和孩子一起给它取名字、让它说话、让它走路，最后带着这些家天使搭一个小小的舞台，演一场“我忘记怎么尿尿了”的戏。

**忘记“应该怎么做”，然后重新做一次。**

这一次，我们想把这个游戏交给孩子。

## 二、具体实施过程

### 1. 画画

邀请小朋友画“你忘记怎么尿尿了”。

画可以是真实的，也可以完全来自想象

### 2. 缝一个天使娃娃

我们准备布料、旧衣物、线等材料，和小朋友一起缝制天使娃娃。

娃娃的肚子会留出一个“小相框”，把小朋友画放进去。

**一幅画变成娃娃的身体。**

### 3. 一起过家家

娃娃做好以后，真正的游戏才开始。

小朋友可以给天使娃娃取名字，决定它是谁、住在哪里、喜欢什么。

我们一起让娃娃走路、说话、吃饭、睡觉、旅行、忘记怎么尿尿。

也许几个天使娃娃会成为一家人，也许它们会成为邻居，也许它们决定一起离开家。

这些都可以。

### 4. 演一场小小的戏

最后，我们和小朋友一起搭一个简单的舞台。

不需要完整的剧本，也不需要专业的表演。

如果我们“忘记怎么尿尿了”，会发生什么？

孩子带着自己的天使娃娃上台，让它们彼此遇见。

一群孩子、一群娃娃、一个临时搭起来的小舞台，就组成了一个过家家。

过家家本来就是儿童重新发明世界规则的游戏。

这就是东村新妇想做的“过家家”——
把假的当真，把小小的游戏变成真的戏。
text.en:
# Project / Activity Name

** "I forgot how to pee" **

# I, theme interpretation

It's a small game.

With a few pieces of paper, a cloth and a chair, the children can pretend that this is a home; the East Village New Woman has been “passing home”.

We set up a temporary table to pretend it's the theatre; pick up a puppet and pretend it's an actor; turn a bed into a stage, turn old cloth into clothes, and turn what is visible in life into drama.

A child suddenly said:

> ** "Forget to pee"**
> **?”**

It's not asking for a physical move, it's asking:

** How should my body exist? **

Because we've been learning a set of social rules about the body since childhood.

Since when does a child know:

This is right. This is wrong.

Here you go. There you go.

This action can be seen, it must be hidden;

This body should be used this way, that body should be used that way.

And when we forget these rules for the time being, will we get a chance to think about life again?

So the Angel doll became a very small experiment:

We want to continue this game with the kids.

** "An angel doll" is a family toy we made together. **

We invited the children to draw a painting first. It can be real, it can come from imagination. Then we sewd a doll of angels with fabric and needles and sewd the children's drawings into it.

The doll's belly is like a little frame with a child's painting in it.

Angel doll is the easiest doll to make.

It can be held up, it can be taken home, it can be an actor.

We'll name it with the kids, let it talk, let it walk, and then we'll put these angels on a little stage and play "I forgot how to pee."

** Forget what to do and do it again. **

This time, we want to give this game to the kids.

# # # II. Implementation process

1. Paint

"You forgot how to pee."

It can be real, it can come from imagination.

# 2. Sew an angel doll #

We've prepared fabrics, old clothes, wires, etc., and sewed angel dolls with kids.

The baby's belly leaves a little picture frame and puts the little ones in.

** A painting becomes the body of a doll. **

# 3. We live together

When the doll is done, the real game begins.

Kids can name the angel doll, decide who it is, where it lives, what it likes.

Together we let the doll walk, talk, eat, sleep, travel and forget how to pee.

Maybe some angel dolls will become a family, maybe they'll become neighbours, maybe they'll decide to leave the house together.

All of this.

# 4. Play a little play

Finally, we set up a simple stage with the kids.

No complete script, no professional performance.

What happens if we forget how to pee?

The children came up with their angel dolls and let them meet each other.

A group of children, a group of dolls, a small stage built up on a temporary basis formed a family.

It's a game where children recreate world rules.

That's what the East Village New Woman wants to do.
Take it seriously, make a little game real.

去年在无墙，我时常听到有人问小朋友“你要去一下厕所吗”？我也时常问自己“我现在要不要趁机去一下厕所？” 东村新妇漂流中，也时常在找一个可以尿尿的地方。如果人类不需要去尿尿就好了？如果我暂时忘记怎么尿尿就好了。“尿尿”于此并不是一个生理上的需求，而是一个符合社会期待的形状。

“你像尿完不拉拉链的臭男人，而我是不拉拉链尿的人。” 



【接力写作】
text.en:
Last year, in a wallless place, I often heard people say, "Do you want to go to the bathroom?" I often ask myself, "Do I need to go to the bathroom now?" The new woman in Toshimura is drifting, and sometimes looking for a place to pee. If only humans didn't have to pee? If only I'd forgotten how to pee for a while. It is not a biological need, but a shape that meets social expectations.

"You're like a stinking man who pees no zipper, and I'm the one who doesn't pee."



"Conduct writing"

text.zh:
东村新妇实验剧团借鉴并承袭了传统潮剧戏班的生存智慧，将“山寨”作为其核心方法论。剧团的灵感源自传承数百年的潮剧——从前，潮剧艺人四海为家，走街串巷，将行头、乐器和道具收进寥寥几口戏箱，每到一处便就地搭台唱戏。虽然“山寨”一词常有模仿、抄袭的意味，但东村新妇将其视作一种灵活变通、集体自组织的草根精神。正如那些围绕既有内容传播，并对其进行重新诠释与延伸的“次生内容”一样，山寨剧团不认为戏剧存在固定不变的定本，而是将其视为在流变、交汇与在地参与中不断重构自身的事物。这种四处辗转的生活方式，至今依然像一条关键的纽带，将如今的潮汕后人与昔日涉海迁徙、文化交融的历史紧紧维系在一起。

通过巡回流动、公开招募、就地搭台与在地协作，东村新妇实验剧团深入不同的空间与社群进行创作演出。剧团成员往往身兼数职，她们既是木偶师，也是木匠；既是乐手，也是司机；既是编剧，也是厨师。除艺术实践外，剧团还实行“漂流经济模式”，在各地建立工作坊、手工艺品生产与演出相结合的循环系统，使劳动变得可见，并让劳动者直接获得报酬。在这种模式中，追求艺术与维持生计不再非此即彼，而是互为表里、相互支撑。今年夏天，剧场将通过“山寨MFA”项目在上海招募一支全新的戏班，招募启事将于七月发布。参与者们将共同组建一个临时剧团，在一起学习、排演、登台，让这场集体协作的戏剧实验持续演进。

关于艺术家：

东村新妇实验剧团是一个开放且流动性的表演团体，发源于中国揭阳的东村。剧团以县镇女性的生活经验与现实处境为创作核心，将传统表演形式转化为当代表达的载体。其创作深受潮州铁枝木偶戏（Iron Rod Puppet）、民间仪式及揭阳“新正顺”木偶剧团工作方式的启发；而在历史上，潮汕木偶戏本身便源自对真人潮剧的模仿、转化与浓缩。

承袭此种“在模仿中生成”的逻辑，剧团将“山寨”视为一种民俗创作方法论：它关乎改写、即兴表演与再创造，而非简单的复制、抄袭。在早期的一次表演中，苗子祖母过世后留下的空床被改造成一个私密的、可移动的木偶戏台。它成为一个与日常现实并行的叙事空间，承载着村中女性的故事、记忆与生活经验。

苗子，“山寨MFA”的发起人之一，一直积极参与该项目的仪式、表演和实验。她还曾发起“东村新妇”、“拿爱去做俱乐部”、“都市麒麟”等艺术实践项目。这些实践以所谓“DIY传统习俗”为方法路径，以草根文化生产方法为基础，依托集体参与与本土知识，对既有文化形态进行重塑，并持续重构传统习俗、地方戏曲及本地民俗文化。
text.en:
The East Village Experimental Women ' s Theatre builds on and inherits the survival wisdom of the traditional tide theatres, using the “savage” as its core methodology. The troupe's inspiration came from hundreds of years of tide dramas. Once upon a time, the twilight performers used to be home, walking through the streets, bringing in a few playboxes, musical instruments and props, where they were staged whenever they arrived. Although the term “savage” is often imitated and copied, the new woman in Toshimura sees it as a grass-roots spirit of flexibility and collective organization. Just as it is about existing content and its reinterpretation and extension of “subsequent content”, the troupe does not believe that the drama has a fixed finality, but rather sees it as a constant re-engineering of itself in fluidity, convergence and local participation. This tumultuous way of life continues to be a key bond that binds today ' s twilight generations with the history of past migration and cultural convergence.

Through mobile tours, open recruitment, local networking and collaboration, the East Village Experimental Theatre for New Women reaches different spaces and communities for creative performances. The members of the theatre are often both puppets and carpenters; musicians and drivers; and writers and cooks. In addition to the practice of art, the troupe also operates a “drive economy model” whereby workshops, handicrafts and performances are set up in various localities, making work visible and paying workers directly. In this model, the pursuit of the arts and the maintenance of livelihoods are no longer the same, but rather the same. This summer, the theatre will recruit an entirely new theatre class in Shanghai through the MFA project, which will be launched in July. Together, participants will form a temporary theatre group to learn, rehearse and stage together so that this collective theatre experiment can continue to evolve.

For artists:

The East Village Experimental Theatre for New Women is an open and mobile performance group that originated in Totomura, China. The theatres focus on the life experiences and realities of women in county towns, transforming traditional forms of performance into a vehicle for contemporary expression. Its creation was inspired by the Iron Rod Puppet, folk rituals and the way in which the “New and Right” puppet theatres worked; historically, the twilight puppet theatre itself originated from the imitation, transformation and enrichment of the reality dramas.

Inherent in this logic of “in imitation”, the troupe sees the “shelter” as a popular method of creation: it is about rewriting, improvisation and creation, not simply copying and copying. In an early performance, the empty bed left behind by the grandmother of Sakako was transformed into a private, mobile puppet stage. It has become a narrative space that goes hand in hand with everyday realities, carrying stories, memories and life experiences of women in villages.

Sakako, one of the founders of the “MFA of the Shan”, has been actively involved in the ceremonies, performances and experiments of the project. She has also initiated the “New Woman in the East Village”, “The Love to the Club” and “The City Baron” art practice projects. These practices are guided by the so-called “DIY traditional practices” and are based on grass-roots cultural production methods, collective participation and indigenous knowledge, reshaping existing cultural patterns and constantly re-establishing traditional practices, local plays and local folklore.

Usually, an art project asks or is asked “what to do”, and most of the “how” is actually a “how to say”.

The troupe isn't an art project, we are a grass-roots team more than the troupe, and the troupe is not going to do what it does, or sometimes not do what it does. Like the traditional tide troupe, 1. performances are not for people, nor are they for the Prince; 2. No restaurants, no cooks; 3. No hotels, no bed; 4. No beef**

Or just "no..."

李洁娜在上次离开上海前说，她应该再也不会来这儿了。我还没见过李洁娜，那我说说其他人的故事。



从我记事以来，阿花就爱做手工鞋，工业的鞋底超过五厘米，鞋面上大朵大朵钩针出来的花，偏执得大块使用紫色，再偏执把鞋子频繁送往小孩的家里，年复一年它们每一双都那么新。挤满别人的鞋柜，也被冷眼相待后，她不再制作手工鞋。阿花的本名里面有“银”也有“花”，老伴病重在上海住院，她站在Cucci店前和广告、标语以及花坛花合影。她穿橘色印花长袖（上面散落着Cucci的标志），红色背心（领口是白色圆点，腰际是略微抽象的烟花）、黑裤子、塑料平底鞋还有金项链。

除了大女儿做过缝纫工，现在在卖跨国缝纫机。没有人和她讨论缝纫，家人没有、村里没有、电视机里也没有。她的儿子来看她，就去隔壁村里的服装店买一双20块钱的帆布鞋，不知道买这么频繁到底给谁穿，但是独居老人的邻里关系是这么打点的。阿花卖烟，熟客让她便宜五毛，她不肯，烟卖不完剩下的自己抽完。阿花每天睡前会用椅子搭舞台，一把一把的椅子接龙抵着临街的门。她的仪式和造景。阿花不认得我，但我在别人的五七拍照，她走过来说，“我死了你可以拍，其他人就算了”。

阿花的朋友半个世纪前从苏北搬来这个浙北的小县城，坐了三天的船，船票好像是两块五。先坐船到南京、再到上海、再到县城。阿花村口的高铁站一小时可以到虹桥，周末送一车一车消费完都市文化的年轻人来扎营学习昆虫，土地开始围上了新的围墙。阿花的村，以前有座木头做的庙，也是半个世纪前大火把庙给烧了，但是石头做的地基还在，绕着村子里的田地、旅游和未拆迁的房子转。“神仙不用庙，神仙住在比人高的树上。”



这些在全球化的工厂外失去织布机的老妇们，和这些在飞机铁路上失去神明的新妇们，两眼相望，也唱不出歌来。山寨李洁娜，还是成为儿童团长。

text.zh:
第一章 《山寨MFA》


第二章《 东村》


李洁娜年轻的时候并没有想做潮剧，尽管父亲就是潮剧团的团长。那个年代拿着钉珠刺绣的手工活到家里干，头家收了货欠钱是常有的事情，可是明天就是过年，两口子口袋翻了个遍就只有二十块。李阿姨和李先生四目相对泪汪汪，在家里坐着不知道怎么办。这时候接到消息（那时候应该还没有电话），一桩白事锣鼓队缺人手，两口子马上带上小儿子一家三口子去帮衬，到晚上回来就有了两百块钱。第二天买只鹅过年，剩下的还能给俩小孩发红包。自此李洁娜决定干潮剧团。“揭阳新正顺潮剧团”已运营三十多年。常年活跃于潮汕寺庙祭神，丧葬等民俗活动，忙的时候要同时组织六七班剧团。

夜晚的戏台总是亮的。虫女小丝带着蛾之身停在台下，说是停其实是偷偷地躲，扬琴的声音每晚都编织出一张网，小丝的翅膀绒毛在网里因为静电而微微膨胀。她也总是去撞深波，让她回忆起曾经撞上过碗中的两颗熟鸡蛋。但说是躲，其实是拜师学艺。

小丝正听得入迷，被竹节虫的前肢戳到，一扭头发现其他生物也聚集在周围，痴痴地听这新正顺潮剧团的演出。小丝爱《八仙过海》，虫如八仙，有各自的本领，住在不同的地方，有着不同的声音。虫子们有的用翅膀打节拍，有的跟着鸣唱，有的跳舞。小丝向她的孩子小小丝讲述这个故事，小小丝们在茧里把故事织了又织，排了又排，虫女们也有了自己的《八虫过海》。

说到过海——三十年后，李洁娜一家在台风白海豚里吞云吐雾，最后折返回家。于是请伯公老爷来保佑，伯公真地道，于是这会你如果偷偷钻进后台来，还能吃到李阿姨从潮汕伯公庙里来的苹果橘子蜜枣……一只白海豚是不够的，潮汕人喜双数。第二只白海豚在木地板上敲敲打打，小动作一出又是一出。这儿人好多、虫好多、却没见到几只夜行的老鼠，夜里没人睡得着。戏台上、戏台后、戏台前的，需要聚精会神吗？


“大风大雨让水快涨到六合彩苗家的门槛，所有的生物们都往高处迁徙。小丝看到蚂蚁在树叶上飘到马路对面；蚊子用侧飞翻滚的方式躲避雨珠；蝴蝶会用翅膀上的鳞片防水……”
——东村今日剧目《八虫过海》 


李洁娜在潮汕经营了四个潮剧团，对眼前这些走来走去的虫女已经不再意外，即使她们破破的手艺是在戏台底下偷学来的，她还是愿意再教教她们，但得用潮汕话。当然虫女们最擅长的还是竖起耳朵偷听，以下是某只小虫偷听来的对话：

苗：这次旅程和以往有啥不同？
娜：平时我没去过这么远的地方，这么老，没坐过飞机，没出过潮汕，这次出来心情特别好，特别是昨天我们说要出去洗澡，出去吃饭，我以前想都不敢想的事情。和你们这些人见面，是我人生的第一次，不会再有第二次了。
苗：怎么会呢？只能说不知道下次是什么时候
娜：不会有的了，我来到这里感觉自己傻得像只鸭子，哈哈哈，不说了
…
苗：你们剧团出动的时候不也是在旅途中吗？
娜：是的，这次我每天跟着大家聊东聊西，回酒店就什么事都不用做，我平时出门心情都很复杂很劳累，要负责全部人的住宿，吃饭，这次完全不同，换做是其他人安排了。
…
苗：那大家瞎敲乐器，你没嫌吵？
娜：哪会！换我老公肯定说“这帮人疯了”，但我好动，心里痒痒得很，也想冲进去跟着敲！
…
虫：为何做剧团是因为喜欢艺术吗？
娜：不，因为做别的工作经常被欠钱，但谁都不敢欠潮剧团的钱。

Chapter I "MFA "


Chapter II East Village


When Lee Jenna was young, she didn't want to do the tide show, even though her father was the head of the tide show. 我不是很擅长写文字，我擅长说话，虽然好像也是自封的，因为我经常跑题，或许我应该说我喜欢说话，喜欢的部分原因可能是因为说话的时候脑袋是放松的。

来前有些小忐忑，想到很多事和想玩的，同时一些人很久没重聚了，也不知道这次开心多还是吵架多——但早已习惯了，或许大家回自己原生父母家也差不多，一种熟悉和紧张，但时间长了可能还是要回一次，这些事不足以让我紧张了。习惯不一定是好事，另一个习惯让我感到很紧张，就是习惯来途还在赶马上要分享的内容，而且也不一定赶得完，但总觉得反正也山寨没事，好像大家都这样。 果然现场也没啥事，得知改成聊天和半剧场形式后觉得赶工成功做的很完美也不一定用得上，一边松口气，一边用惯常的笨蛋方式适应着现场。

一次又一次，好像都没啥事，有事了也能大事化小，小事化了。好像前面的紧张也是给现场爆发即兴能量蓄力，也是没办法（总是很多事最后才发现没搞精力时间做好了呀！），最后升华到对世道无常的接受（羔羊一般）。这些事在山寨（还有各种姊妹的神经发散活动）里在常不过了。 不如甚至说山寨正当化了这种状况的美感。

面对压力所呈现的紧——松关系， 压力积攒——很紧很紧——然后突然断线，松驰，心情大释怀——这究竟是个什么样的循环啊？ 光听听就上瘾，像一种过山车的上升，暑假前夕的期末考、高考、自慰、赶ddl、我去，是不是我们贯穿亚b（东亚人）一生啊，难怪这么欲罢不能？ 感觉越来越擅长这些的过程，也越来越担心了——这样的范式曾推进过不少的创作，会不会已经对这个模式上瘾了？？如果它成了我们输出创造和批判的主要过程，手忙脚乱是不是就成了我们的盲区和瓶颈，来不及做好的就等于永远没有，好像也挺损耗一个事的潜力的？ 更不用提带来的健康代价……躺平吧，又觉得一切又都无所谓了…

想做的事和结果之间好像总是有些偏航，有点像喝醉的人。想起自己小时候喝醉最大的兴趣就是学习表演普通人，如果我希望抬手臂的力度是3，烂醉下我抬的是9，我的策略就是可以把力道调成1，这样外面的人都不知道我喝醉了。一时还好，总这样也挺累的，我也不太清楚该不该太控制。想控制是不是因为没醉的彻底？还是因为不醉就好了？或者两者都有？从这个循环过程中走出不容易，或许需要大家积思广义。如何临危不乱轻松工作，输出一切如automode？我擦。 脑袋放松的前提是身体放松，身体放松的前提，是多动动，多按摩！然后多休息。

幾年前，我在潮汕經過一處裝修工地，到處是泥土、灰塵、機械、鋼筋、轟鳴，人們在髒亂和擁擠里穿行。幾個工人在角落擺出一套很小的茶具。坐著歇息。

當時我並沒有特別印象。我想去很遠的地方。

多年後，我去了泰北的香巴拉。那裡聚集著來自世界各地的人，到處是手工、嬉皮、薩滿、儀式、音樂、神秘。

我參加了一個冥想工作坊。帶領者是個高大、粗壯、安靜的白人。

突然我注意到，我們坐著的，是一塊藍白紅的塑料編織布，和中國工地常見的那種基本一模一樣。

整個營地地上都是泥和碎石，那塊塑料布讓人很舒服。

冥想結束後，我跟他說起那塊塑料布，說起很多年前在潮汕見過的那套小茶具：工地中央，人們在噪音和灰塵里怎樣一口一口喝茶。

他被打動了。幾天後的深夜，我去露天廁所時，又碰見了他。他和一個我認識的女人站在廁所外，氣氛有點尷尬，我有點慌張，他反而沒有什麼緊張。我們打了招呼後，他忽然很認真地向她重新講起我說過的那個潮汕故事。

夜裡的廁所旁，一個白人男人認真談論中國工地上的茶，沒有拉下一個細節。像在一口一口慢慢喝茶。

許久，我們說完，我進去廁所尿尿了。我停在那，看到一條小溪。也像是茶。

這個月在上海，在市中心的藝術空間，我一次次看到李阿姨她們在靜靜地喝茶。

劇團後台有時候像個工地，Commons Station 的中文名似乎就是共/工地，大大地寫在牆上。上海辦公室和各種空間都很乾淨，我們把它們變成了工地。物品四散，人情擁擠，感受轟鳴，思想雜亂，倫理道德，揚塵四起，靈魂泥沙俱下。

神明也在其中嗎？我只知道潮劇和很多地方戲是演給神明的，神在一座廟，神在一座雕像，神在一個節慶儀式，神在一個時辰，一個敬拜和祈求，一個瞬間。cherub 好像是小天使的意思，也是神明的使者。真的嗎？

在Cheruby門口表演時，在上海市中心街上洶湧人潮中停下來，能感覺到自己的停下，時間的停下，而自己停在安靜屋裡卻容易忘記自己的停。

後台前台人流的陰晴變換中，似乎總有一絲神秘縈繞其中。我想這裡原本是最適合停下來的地方。

只要停下來，就能看到那神秘的命運之手在如何操控我們這些人偶。只要看到祂，也就不必看到別的什麼，也不必被人看到。

我想那些我們操控的偶也可以有停下的瞬間。

好像幾乎沒有。我扮演昆蟲，雙腳搭在Cheruby門口的共享單車上，和Denni在鬥蛐蛐。搖搖欲墜間，我沒有讓昆蟲讓自己停下來哪怕一個呼吸。

我一直在搖搖欲墜，就像偶。

我們的偶被布縫出。情緒的正面和負面，像是一塊布的正反，有些人在反面密密縫製，外人看到，透過輕薄布料，能看出出朦朧的暗影與輪廓，感受到神秘，感受到美。感受不到正面負面。

我想起那塊塑料布，坐在那裡很好。感受到美。

只要那樣坐著，不論我眼睛看向哪裡，都有或曾有媽媽，都有零星散布的記憶巨石，和傍晚薄薄的一層思緒萬千般地細雨，雨滴在我全身上下周圍敲得小小的啪嗒響。

阿超的情緒有種潮濕泥土的腥氣，在我全身上下周圍飄著。她的愛像是有黏軟又熱乎的沙子，能讓人沒完沒了地走下去。還有大大小小的人，數著有幾張椅子空了沒人坐，在那裡摸索不在的形狀。

白海豚之後的上海，劇團裡有一種溫熱的氣氛，在退進模糊發黑的暗處，跟著我緩慢、有時笨重拖沓的步子，有節奏地一下一下跳動。明白有時在樓梯的拐角關切地問我怎麼樣。我感動。而我總是跑去廁所撒尿。但是撒尿途中也從沒停下來。

此刻我想，如果我曾停下來，我會想到一條小溪。

小溪滿足地流過那些曾經扎人、硌手的尖石。如果我把雙手像翅膀一樣向兩側展開，就能觸碰到兩岸。

title.zh: 在集体实践中重新理解创作 东村新妇潮剧团上海行反思
title.en: In collective practice, re-understanding the idea of creating a new women's play in Toshimura.

text.zh:
东村新妇潮剧团 · 上海日记

	我们一直在道歉和道谢

	上海披了一层西方的皮，但我最欣赏的那部分，人文精神，在这次经历里，我很少感受到。在美国，我与社会地位比我高的人交流时，往往感受不到那么强的等级差异。至少在相处的那一刻，我不会不断意识到谁有资源、谁有权力、谁应该听话。在这里，这些权利意识却被反复强调。
	
	我们没有听到一句“谢谢你们的表演”，收到的是：不守规矩，服装奇怪，行为奇怪。我们被要求符合框架，学习那些被认为优秀、符合传统的人是怎么做事的。

	但我们的行为不是凭空发生的，都有各自的来处。我们只是带着勇气和想象力，把自己理解、相信的东西继续往外拓展。

	“开始你们都不听，后来你们都好乖啊。”我们来到这个空间，到底被当成了什么？一起工作、一起创作的人，还是需要被管教，最后终于学会听话的人？“好乖”我们的付出、判断和创造，好像最后都被归结成了服从。“他的行为有文化背书，所以他是成立的。”	我很震惊，这会是一个文化组织说出来的话。一个行为必须先有某种被认可的文化替它背书，才能成立吗？那些还没有得到认可的尝试，又该在哪里发生？

	东村新妇一直承受着太多来自固有阶层和标准的审视。但我们做的事，也在参与这个社会：让人相遇，让关系发生，让习以为常的约定俗成规则有机会被重新看见。然而这些劳动为什么总是被轻视。“少数服从多数”就是其实是最差的一条
	
	我不想再习惯性地道歉和道谢了。我们没有把事情搞砸，我们把很多事情做得精彩、出色。得到空间和资源，不应该意味着我们必须接受居高临下的对待。
	
	我们的攻击力也应该有向外的出口，去回应那些让我们受伤的规则和态度。
	
	这一次，我想把感谢还给我们自己。谢谢我们做出的衣服、道具和表演，谢谢我们的勇气、想象力和付出。我们值得欣赏自己，尊重自己，也值得给到一句：谢谢我们的表演。

	我们有二十多个人，有熟悉的，也有不熟悉的。馆方说我们把尿渍留在了厕所外面，但具体是谁、怎么发生的. 我并不清楚，我们也没有在管理每个人怎么上厕所。
	
	而馆方在开会时，当着大家的面，自顾自地吃起了肯德基。在我看来，这种不顾他人感受的行为，同样是不尊重人。为什么我们的行为会被拿出来说，他们的行为却好像不需要被讨论？所谓的规矩，是大家一起遵守，还是有些人负责制定，另一些人负责服从？

	这也让我想到，我们做的事情，本来就在测试这些框架。社会和机构的框架，也可以被测试、被质疑、被改变。我们通过衣服、身体和表演，去碰一碰那些平时没有人说出来的界限：为什么这样穿就奇怪？为什么这样行动就不合适？一个人必须先有文化背书，他的表达才值得被认真对？

	我们也在测试大家习惯了的看法。什么被认为正常，什么被认为有文化，什么又会被当成没有素质。这些判断到底从哪里来？换一个身份、换一个有资源的人做同样的事，得到的评价会不会不一样？
text.en:
Toshimura New Women's Tide. Shanghai Day. Remember

We've been apologizing and thanking.

Shanghai is covered with Western skins, but the human spirit, the part that I admire most, has rarely been felt in this experience. In the United States, when I speak to people in higher social status than I do, I often do not feel so much hierarchy. At least for the moment when we are together, I will not constantly realize who has resources, who has power and who should listen. Here, however, the awareness of these rights is repeatedly emphasized.
	
We didn't hear the phrase “thank you for your performance”, and we received the message that there was no discipline, strange costumes, strange behavior. We are asked to conform to the framework and to learn how people who are considered to be good and who are in line with tradition do things.

But our actions do not take place in a vacuum; they have their own places. We only continue to expand what we understand and believe with courage and imagination.

"You didn't listen at first, and then you were good." What have we come to this space for? Is there someone who works together, who creates together, who needs discipline and who finally learns to listen? “Be good” our work, judgment, and creation seem to end up as submissive. “His actions were culturally endorsed, so he was established.” I am shocked that this is what a cultural organization says. Does an act have to be endorsed by a recognized culture before it can be established? Where should those unacknowledged attempts take place?

The East Village New Women have been subjected to too much scrutiny from inherent classes and standards. But what we do is also participating in this society: meeting people, making relationships happen, giving the usual conventional rules a chance to be seen again. But why are these jobs always being despised? "minority obeys majority" is actually the worst.
	
I don't want to be used to apologies and thanks. We did not screw things up, and we did a lot of good and good. Access to space and resources should not mean that we have to accept subservient treatment.
	
Our offensive power should also be exported to respond to the rules and attitudes that hurt us.
	
This time, I want to give thanks back to ourselves. Thank you for our clothes, props and performances, for our courage, imagination and dedication. We deserve to appreciate ourselves, respect ourselves, and a word: thank you for our performance.

We have more than 20 people, both familiar and unfamiliar. They said we left the piss stain outside the toilet, but who and how did it happen?
	
And during the meeting, the museum ate Kentucky in front of everyone. In my view, this disregard for the feelings of others is equally disrespectful. Why are our actions to be told and their actions not to be discussed? Are the rules to be followed together or are some responsible for making them up and others for obeying them?

It also reminds me that what we do is already testing these frameworks. The social and institutional framework can also be tested, challenged and changed. We go through clothes, bodies and performances to touch the boundaries that no one normally says: why is it so strange? Why is this not appropriate? A man must have a cultural endorsement before his expression is worthy of serious consideration?

We're also testing what you're used to. What is considered normal, what is considered cultural and what is considered to be lack of quality. Where exactly are these judgments coming from? Would it not be the same thing to do the same thing with another identity and another resourceful person?

text.zh:
大课间 8月8日-9日

最早的过家家记忆是医院，场景灰暗，四五个小朋友一组。过家家的竞争性在开场的角色挑选，我的建议是选第二高人气的角色，多少有种鹬蚌相争，第二名保存体力的心态。那医院过家家，人气第二名是谁？自己和自己的过家家，是在变成大人的过程中克服恐惧的小聪明——坐在厕所里打电话给门外信任的大人，练习和陌生人的隔空对谈。我最近在练习写小说，都说多看小说可以锻炼自己的写作，但我却对小说家的采访入了迷，如果我山寨小说家写作的姿态、谈论出版的犹豫和决心以及和编辑、出版社的来回交锋，不久后我就会变成小说家吗？好像并不是。我还是惧怕写作本身，因为我的虚构故事材料里，都是别人的秘密。比如此刻，我感受到了蓬勃而生的灾难感，土耳其男孩从家里的阳台给妈妈和妹妹扔下小包调味料却因为风力不足而飘进了邻居的阳台，没有牵绳子的狗差点冲进街道在最后一刻被叫住，我的电动滑板车方向盘并没有那么灵敏，有人大吼争吵着穿过红绿灯——而我闻到的是童年放学厨房里面的味道。一切都是被闷蒸包裹着大泡沫纸袋。

厕所里的电话响了！ 

小雨打电话来说，自己对山寨的语言还不熟悉，她想在来上海的路上做遗憾收集计划。菜菜也打电话来说，他在东村哭了一下，也许他没有离开绘画而是在东村暂时离开了对画家身份的服从。麻烦精跟着空心人的脚步漂流回海上，一路上，它和白色面孔的人说起山寨精神，他们纷纷点头表示理解，但麻烦精自己却变得更加犹豫不决。是时候把照面再打一打，上上山寨思想品德课，没有老师也没有鹬蚌。

我忘记把这支号码留给李洁娜。李洁娜在上次离开上海前说，她应该再也不会来这儿了。那天，电话没有拨出去，七岁的儿童团长看着满屋的大人、乐器，问了一句谁是团长。儿童团长站在李洁娜旁边，在余下他人的同一个十点钟方向。

我还没见过李洁娜和儿童团长，那我再说说其他人的故事。

从我记事以来，阿花就爱做手工鞋，工业的鞋底超过五厘米，鞋面上大朵大朵钩针出来的花，偏执得大块使用紫色，再偏执把鞋子频繁送往小孩的家里，年复一年它们每一双都那么新。挤满别人的鞋柜，也被冷眼相待后，她不再制作手工鞋。阿花的本名里面有“银”也有“花”，老伴病重在上海住院，她站在Cucci店前和广告、标语以及花坛花合影。她穿橘色印花长袖（上面散落着Cucci的标志），红色背心（领口是白色圆点，腰际是略微抽象的烟花）、黑裤子、塑料平底鞋还有金项链。

除了大女儿做过缝纫工，现在在卖跨国缝纫机。没有人和她讨论缝纫，家人没有、村里没有、电视机里也没有。她的儿子来看她，就去隔壁村里的服装店买一双20块钱的帆布鞋，不知道买这么频繁到底给谁穿，但是独居老人的邻里关系是这么打点的。阿花卖烟，熟客让她便宜五毛，她不肯，烟卖不完剩下的自己抽完。阿花每天睡前会用椅子搭舞台，一把一把的椅子接龙抵着临街的门。她的仪式和造景。阿花不认得我，但我在别人的五七拍照，她走过来说，“我死了你可以拍，其他人就算了”。

阿花的朋友半个世纪前从苏北搬来这个浙北的小县城，坐了三天的船，船票好像是两块五。先坐船到南京、再到上海、再到县城。阿花村口的高铁站一小时可以到虹桥，周末送一车一车消费完都市文化的年轻人来扎营学习昆虫，土地开始围上了新的围墙。阿花的村，以前有座木头做的庙，也是半个世纪前大火把庙给烧了，但是石头做的地基还在，绕着村子里的田地、旅游和未拆迁的房子转。“神仙不用庙，神仙住在比人高的树上。”

这些在全球化的工厂外失去织布机的老妇们，和这些在飞机铁路上失去神明的新妇们，两眼相望，也唱不出歌来。山寨李洁娜，还是成为儿童团长。



 

 

 

 

8月8日，11:00 山寨团魂：思想品德课

山寨方法论：

介绍中文领域的“山寨”，以及英文领域的“海盗\盗版（pirate）”语义和所指相关的发展史 ，以及在不同时空、文化领域中两者交织的草根实践。

盗版（pirate）在欧洲行动者社群中常作为一个带有罗宾汉侠盗色彩的词汇；另一方面，这个词在大型文化资本，以及涉及版权的行业中备受骂名。

“pirate”这词原本的指的海盗，他们的形象也一直和文化行业里的pirate类似的冲突。无论对外的形象有多肆虐，海盗成员之间似乎的关系似乎没有想象的那么差， 甚至有人类学学者指出海盗或许是欧洲保险制度和民主制度的起源。

山寨也很像原本指的是山里具有防御功能的寨子，后来也指穷人之地。 到后来水浒传中的梁山好汉将其基地称之为“山寨”，这个词汇就蒙上了“草根自组织”的色彩。随着改革开放，它的发展变得越发越有搞笑色彩...（黄译）

咱們這些個野路子，要是撿到點兒什麼機會啦，像什麼展覽、經費、對談會之類的。咱們得把那些光鮮亮麗的「資源」掰碎了、搗爛了，盡可能地往外撒，搞點兒分享啊、再分配啊，讓那些個平常沒啥這種機會的，也能分一杯羹！因為啊，那些不被看到的人，他們骨子裡頭那股子山寨的精氣神兒，可比咱們這些個自稱「山寨」的更濃烈！（jojo）

提到山寨理论，很多人都会想到韩炳哲写的《山寨-中国式解析》这本书。书中描述的中国，绝不是我们这一代人所经历的那个正在迅速现代化的中国。我想大多数受过现代教育的年轻人都对中国传统多少有些不屑。它们总是让我联想到那些互相吹捧的长辈。这本来也没什么好说的，直到我们看到了更加死气沉沉的当代艺术。

《山寨》的最后一章探讨了“山寨（假货/仿造）”本身。与前面提到的中国画不同，传统艺术虽然正在衰落，但至少是被认可的艺术。然而，“山寨”指代的却是那些从未被摆上台面的事物。我认为它甚至可以是一个人的“山寨”，比如为了谋生而进行的街头表演，我想就算是一瞬间的民俗也是民俗吧。

两年前我深圳的除夕夜遇到了这一幕。与传统中那些气势磅礴的舞狮队不同，这场单人舞狮在街头上似乎并不怎么受欢迎，他挨家挨户讨赏，我很想找出来分享给大家，但视频已经过期，只留下这张背影，我想我会永远记住他，从狮子嘴巴露出来的疲惫笑脸，动作中也流露出一种卑微的姿态，同时却又是整条街最勇敢的人。

这几年我山寨过纳西麒麟戏的木老师，摩梭东巴阿公塔，还有新正顺木偶剧团的团长李洁娜。总之我觉得和山寨对象相处，山寨思想品德课还蛮重要的。

(六合彩苗)

8月9日 14:00 山寨练功：如何成为团长 

"揭阳新正顺潮剧团"，已运营三十多年。团长李洁娜，自幼自学潮剧，后带动全家和村里其他人一起经营了四个剧团，常年活跃于潮汕寺庙祭神，丧葬等民俗活动，问起为何做剧团是因为喜欢艺术吗？答“不，因为做别的工作经常被欠钱，但谁都不敢欠潮剧团的钱。”（潮剧团演出几乎都是民俗活动，先由村理事会向村民筹款，筹到款后才请剧团。）

本课程将由李洁娜团长亲自传授三十年民间草根组织的经验。

由于山寨剧团现任团长只有7岁，为了谨慎起见，我们将正式成立一个团长智囊团，有兴趣的加入团长智囊团并之后继续漂流的千万不要错过这节课。

 



 

 

大课间可以指：

1. 山寨MFA学校公开的课间游戏和仪式，开放对山寨学校好奇但是站在栏杆外的家长、亲朋好友或者路人，也是消化排练中即兴产生的表演欲望和对话空间的时段。
2. 比普通课间十分钟更长的“调整”时间段，舞台可以重新制景、演员可以转换角色、故事也可以重新再讲一遍。我们也可以坐下来，再读一次剧本。
3. “你什么时候发现自己的身体的？”“不算是第一次，但是中学大课间操，三个学校一起比赛。我和班上最胖的孩子们，被禁止参赛。”

title.zh: 演木偶戏的人 安徒生童话

text.zh:
轮船上有一个年纪相当大的演木偶戏的人。他有一副愉快的面孔。如果他这个面孔的表情是代表实际情况的话，那么他就要算是人世间一个最幸福的人了。他说他正是这样的一个人，而且是我听他亲口这样说的。他是我的同胞——一个丹麦人，他同时也是一个旅行剧团的导演。他的整个班子装在一个大匣子里，因为他是一个演木偶戏的人。他说他有一种天生的愉快心情，而且这种心情还被一个工艺学校的学生“洗涤”过一次。这次实验的结果使他成了一个完全幸福的人。我起初并没有马上就听懂其中的道理，不过他把整个的经过都解释给我听了。下面是全部的经过：
“事情发生在斯拉格尔斯，”他说，“我正在一个邮局的院子里演木偶戏。观众非常不一般——除了两个老太婆以外，全是小孩子。这时有一个学生模样的人，穿着一身黑衣服，走了进来。他坐下来，在适当的时候发笑，在适当的时候鼓掌。他是一个很不平常的看客！我倒很想知道，他究竟是一个什么人。我听说他是哥本哈根工艺学校的一个学生，这次是特别被派到乡下来教育老百姓的。
“我的演出在八点钟就结束了，因为孩子们须得早点上床去睡觉——我不能不考虑观众的习惯。在九点钟的时候，这个学生开始演讲和实验。这时我也成为他的听众之一。又听又看，这真是一桩美妙的事情。像俗话所说的，大部分的东西在我的头上滑过而钻进牧师的脑袋里去了。不过我还是不免起了一点感想：如果我们凡人能够想出这么多东西，我们一定是打算活得很久——比我们在人世间的这点生命总归要久一点。他所实验的这些东西可算是一些小小的奇迹，都做得恰到好处，非常自然。像这样的一个工艺学校学生，在摩西和预言家的时代，一定可以成为国家的一个圣人[插图]；但是假如在中世纪，他无疑会被烧死[插图]。
“我一整夜都没有睡。第二天晚上，当我做第二次演出的时候，这位学生又来了；这时我的心情变得非常好。我曾经从一个演戏的人那儿听到一个故事：据说当他演一个情人的角色的时候，他头脑中总是想着观众中的一个女客。他只是为她而表演，其余的人他都忘得干干净净。现在这位工艺学校的学生就是我的‘她’，我的唯一看客，我真是为‘她’而演戏。等这场戏演完了，所有的木偶都出来谢了幕以后，这位工艺学校的学生就请我到他的房里去喝一杯酒。他谈起我的戏，我谈起他的科学。我相信我们两方面都感到非常满意。不过我还得有些保留，因为他虽然实验了许多东西，但是却说不出一个道理。比如说吧，有一片铁一溜出螺旋形的器具就有了磁性。这是什么道理呢？铁忽然获得了一种精气，但这种精气是从什么地方来的呢？我想这和现实世界里的人差不多：上帝让人在时间的螺旋器具里乱撞，于是精气附在人身上，于是我们便有了一个拿破仑，一个路德，或者类似的人物。
“‘整个的世界是一系列的奇迹，’学生说，‘不过我们已经非常习惯于这些东西，所以我们只是把它们叫作日常事件。’
“于是他侃侃而谈，做了许多解释，直到后来我忽然觉得好像我的头盖骨一下子被揭开了。老实说，要不是现在我已经老了，我马上就要到工艺学校去学习研究这个世界的办法，虽然我现在已经是一个最幸福的人了。
“‘一个最幸福的人！’他说，似乎对我的这句话颇感兴味，‘你是幸福的吗？’
“‘是。’我说，‘我和我的班子无论到什么城市里去，都受到欢迎。当然，我也有一个希望。这个希望常常像一个妖精——一个噩梦——似的来到我心里，把我的好心境打乱。这个希望是：我希望能成为一个真正戏班子的老板，一个真正男演员和女演员的导演。’
“‘你希望你的木偶都有生命，你希望它们都变成活生生的演员。’他说，‘你真的相信，你一旦成了他们的导演，你就会变得绝对幸福吗？’
“他不相信有这个可能，但是我却相信。我们把这个问题从各个方面畅谈了一通，谈来谈去总得不到一致的意见。虽然如此，我们仍然碰了杯——酒真是好极了。酒里一定有某种魔力，否则我就应该醉了。但事实不是这样，我的头脑非常清楚。房间里好像有太阳光——而这太阳光是从这位工艺学校学生的脸上射出来的。这使我想起了古时候的一些神仙，他们永远年轻，周游世界。我把这个意思告诉他，他微笑了一下。我可以发誓，他一定是一个古代的神仙下凡，或者神仙一类的人物。他一定是这样的一个人物：我最高的希望将会得到满足，木偶们将会获得生命，我将成为真正演员的导演。
[插图]
“我们为这事而干杯。他把我的木偶都装进一个木匣子，把这匣子绑在我的背上，然后让我钻进一个螺旋形的器具里去。我现在还可以听得见，我是怎样滚出来、躺在地板上的。这是千真万确的事情，全班的戏子从匣子里跳出来。我们身上全有精气附体了。所有的木偶现在都成了有名的艺术家——这是他们自己讲的，而我自己则成了导演。现在一切都齐备，可以登台表演了。整个的班子都想和我谈谈。观众也是一样。
“女舞蹈家说，如果她不用一只腿立着表演，整个的剧院就会关门；她是整个班子的女主角，同时也希望大家用这个标准来对待她。表演皇后这个角色的女演员希望，在下了舞台以后，大家仍然把她当作皇后看待，否则她的艺术就要生疏了。
“那位专门充当送信人的演员，也好像一个初次恋爱的人一样，做出一副不可一世的样子，因为他说，从艺术的完整性讲，小人物跟大人物是同样重要。男主角要求只演退场的那些场面，因为这些场面会叫观众鼓掌。女主角只愿意在红色灯光下表演，因为只有这种灯光才对她合适——她不愿意在蓝色的灯光下表演。
[插图]
“他们简直像关在瓶子里的一堆苍蝇，而我却不得不跟他们一起挤在这个瓶子里，因为我是他们的导演。我的呼吸停止了，我的头脑昏了，世上再没有什么人像我这样可怜。我现在是生活在一群新的人种中间。我希望能把他们再装进匣子里，我希望我从来没有当过他们的导演。我老老实实地告诉他们说，他们不过是木偶而已。于是他们就把我打得要死。
“我躺在我自己房间里的床上。我是怎样到那儿的，怎样离开那个工艺学校学生的，大概他知道；我自己是不知道的。月光照在地板上；木匣子躺在照着的地方，已经打翻了；大大小小的木偶躺在它的附近，滚作一团。但是我再也不能耽误时间了。我马上从床上跳下来，把它们统统捞进去，有的头朝下，有的用腿站着。我赶快把盖子盖上，在匣子上坐下来。这副样儿是值得画下来的。你能想象出这副样儿吗？我是能的。
“‘现在要请你们待在里面了，’我说，‘我再也不能让你们变得有血有肉了！’
“我感到全身轻松了一截，心情又好起来。我是一个最幸福的人了。这个工艺学校学生算是把我的头脑洗涤一番了。我幸福地坐着，当场就在匣子上睡去了。第二天早晨——事实上是中午，因为这天早晨我意外地睡得久——我仍然坐在匣子上，非常快乐，同时也体会到我以前的那种希望真是太傻。我去打听那个工艺学校的学生，但是他已经像希腊和罗马的神仙一样不见了。从那时起，我一直是一个最幸福的人。
[插图]
“我是一个幸福的导演，我的演员也不再发牢骚了，我的观众也很满意——因为他们尽情地欣赏我的演出。我可以随便安排我的节目，我可以随便把剧本中的最好的部分选出来演，谁也不会因此对我生气。那些三十年前许多人抢着要看而且看得流出眼泪的剧本，我现在都演出来了，虽然现在的一些大戏院都瞧不起它们。我把它们演给小孩子们看，小孩子们流起眼泪来，跟爸爸和妈妈过去没有什么两样。我演出《约翰妮·蒙特法康》和《杜威克》，不过这都是节选，因为小孩子不愿意看拖得太长的恋爱故事。他们喜欢简短和感伤的东西。
“我在丹麦各地都旅行过。我认识所有的人，所有的人也认识我。现在我要到瑞典去了。如果我在那里的运气好、能够赚很多的钱，我就做一个真正的北欧人——否则我就不做了。因为你是我的同乡，所以我才把这话告诉你。”
而我呢，作为他的同胞，自然要把这话马上传达出来——完全没有其他的意思。
(1851)
text.en:
There's a pretty old puppet on board. He has a pleasant face. If his face represents reality, he will be the happiest man on earth. He said he was the same person and I heard him say that. He is my compatriot — a Danish, and he is also the director of a tour theatre. His whole team was in a box because he was a puppet. He said that he had a natural sense of pleasure and that that feeling had been “cleaned” once by students of a craft school. The results of this experiment made him a perfectly happy person. I didn't understand it at first, but he explained the whole story to me. Here's the whole story:
"It happened in Slagles," he said, "I'm playing puppets in a post office yard. Audiences are very unusual -- except for two old ladies, all children. At that time, a student was dressed in black and walked in. He sits down, laughs at the right time, applauds at the right time. He is an extraordinary visitor. I wonder who he is. I heard that he was a student at the Copenhagen Polytechnic School, this time specifically sent to the countryside to educate the population.
“My performance ended at 8:00 because the children had to go to bed early — I couldn't ignore the audience habits. At nine o'clock, the student began to speak and experiment. And then I became one of his listeners. It's a wonderful thing to hear and see. As the saying goes, most things slip over my head and go into the head of a priest. But I can't help but feel that: If we mortals can come up with so much, we must be prepared to live a long life — a little longer than our life in the world. These things he's been experimenting with are a few little miracles, all right, very natural. A student at a craft school like this can certainly be a saint of the country in Moses and Prophethood; but in the Middle Ages he would certainly be burned.
"I haven't slept all night. The next night, when I did my second performance, the student came back; I was in a very good mood. I once heard a story from a actor: It was said that when he played the role of a lover, he was thinking of a woman in his mind. He's just acting for her, and the rest of him forgets everything. And now the students of this craft school are my "she", my only visitors, and I'm acting for her. When the show was over, all the puppets came out and the students at the crafts school invited me to his room for a drink. He talks about my play, I talk about his science. I am sure that we are both very satisfied. But I have some reservations to make, because he's experimenting with a lot of things, but he can't make any sense. For example, there's a piece of iron that slips out of the spiral. What's the point? Iron suddenly acquires a quality, but where does it come from? I think it's like people in the real world: God puts people in a spiral of time, so he's leaning on people, so we have a Napoleon, a Luther, or something like that.
"The whole world is a series of miracles," the student says, "but we're very used to these things, so we call them routine events. I'm sorry.
“Then he talked, and made many explanations, until then I suddenly felt like my skull had been removed. To be honest, if it hadn't been for now, I'd be going to a craft school to study the world's methods, although I'm now the happiest person.
"'A happiest man!' He said, 'Do you feel happy about my words?'
"Yes." I said, "I and my team are welcome in any city. Of course I have a hope too. This hope often comes to me like a leprechaun — a nightmare — and breaks my heart. The hope is: I want to be the boss of a real theatre team, the director of a real actor and actress. I'm sorry.
"'You want your puppets to be alive and you want them to be living actors. He said, "Do you really believe that once you become their director, you will become absolutely happy?"
“He didn't believe in that possibility, but I did. We have talked about this issue in all its aspects, and we have never been able to agree on it. Still, we touched a glass of wine -- that's great. There must be some magic in the wine or I should be drunk. But that's not true. My mind is very clear. There seemed to be sunlight in the room, which had come out of the face of the student at the craft school. This reminds me of ancient wonders who were always young and travelled around the world. I told him that. He smiled. I swear to God, he must be a man of the ancient gods, or something like that. He must be a man whose highest hopes will be fulfilled, whose puppets will be given life and who will be the director of the real actor.
[ Diagrams ]
“We drink to this. He put my puppets in a wooden box, tied it to my back, and then let me drill into a spiral device. I'm okay now. I can hear you. How I got out on the floor. It's true. The whole class jumps out of the box. We've got a whole body of fine air. All the puppets are now famous artists. That's what they say, and I'm the director. Now everything's ready for the show. The whole team wants to talk to me. So does the audience.
“The dancer said that if she did not perform on one leg, the whole theatre would be closed; she was the leading woman in the entire team and wanted to be treated with that standard. The actress who performed the role of Queen hopes that she will still be treated as Queen after the stage, otherwise her art will be lost.
“The actor, who specializes in acting as a messenger, acts as if he were in love for the first time, because he says that, in terms of the integrity of art, small people are as important as big people. The leading man asked for those scenes to be taken off, because they would have the audience applaud. The heroine only wants to perform under the red light, because the only light that suits her - She doesn't want to perform under the blue light.
[ Diagrams ]
"They were like flies in a bottle, and I had to squeeze them in it because I was their director. My breath stopped, my head went out, and there was no one in the world like me. I'm living in a new race. I wish I could put them back in the box, and I wish I'd never been their director. And We told them with truth that they were nothing but puppets. So they beat me to death.
“I lay on the bed of my own room. How did I get there, and how did I leave the students of the Crafts School? He probably knew it; I did not know it myself. The moonlight was on the floor; the wooden box was lying there and had been turned over; the puppets, large and small, were lying near it and rolling around. But I can't take any more time. I jumped off the bed, pulled them all in, some head down, some legs standing. I'll put the lid on and sit down on the box. It's worth drawing. Can you imagine that? I can.
"Now I'm going to ask you to stay inside, and I'm going to say, "I can't let you become flesh and blood anymore!"
"I felt so relieved and feeling better. I'm the happiest man now. The students at this craft school sort of washed my mind. I sat happily and slept on the box. The next morning — in fact, it was noon, because that morning I had an unexpectedly long sleep — I was still sitting on a box, very happy and feeling the same hopes I had before. I went to ask about the students at that craft school, but he was gone like a Greek and a Roman fairy. I've been the happiest man ever since.
[ Diagrams ]
“I am a happy director, and my actors are no longer complaining, and my audience is satisfied — because they appreciate my performance. I can arrange my show, I can choose the best part of the script, nobody gets mad at me. I now perform those scripts that many people had to watch and see tearing tears 30 years ago, even though some of the great theatres now despise them. I showed them to the kids, who cried, like their father and mother. I played "Johnny Montefacon" and "Dweyke," but it was all an option, because kids didn't want to read long love stories. They like short and sad things.
“I have traveled all over Denmark. I know everyone. I know everybody. Now I'm going to Sweden. If I'm lucky there and make a lot of money, I'll be a real Nordic — or I won't do it. Because you're from my hometown, that's why I'm telling you."
And I, as one of his fellow citizens, naturally have to convey it immediately — nothing else.
(1851)

description.zh: 他不称那世界为超自然，而称之为第二注意力（second attention），他身为老师的角色是使这种系统能被我掌握。我在先前的书中描述过他的方法，以及他要我练习的巫术技巧，其中最重要的被他称为“做梦的艺术”。
description.en: He doesn't call the world supernatural, he calls it second attention, and his role as a teacher is to get this system in my hands. I have described his methods in previous books, as well as his witchcraft skills, the most important of which he has called “the art of dreams”.

text.zh: “‘做梦’只能被体验，‘做梦’不只是有梦，也不是白日梦或胡思乱想。透过‘做梦’我们能知觉其他的世界，我们可以描述这些世界，虽然我们无法描述我们如何知觉它们。不过我们可以感觉‘做梦’如何打开那些世界，‘做梦’似乎是一种感知，一种身体中的思考过程，一种心灵中的感官。”
text.en: “Dreams can only be experienced, and dreams are not only dreams, they are not daydreams or delusions. Through "dreaming" we can see the other worlds, we can describe them, although we cannot describe how we perceive them. But we can feel how "dream" opens up those worlds, and "dreaming" seems like a sense, a process of thinking in the body, a sense in the mind."

title.en: The first door to a dream.

description.zh: 摘自《心灵成长与自由意志，做梦的艺术》
description.en: It's from "Breath and Free Will, Art of Dreams."

text.zh: 我们只能有那么多的分量，而我们把它全用在知觉及处理我们那吃人的世界。他再三强调，没有更多的能量可得，而且由于我们能用的能量都已有用途，以至于没有一点可用来进行任何不寻常的特异知觉，譬如说做梦。“那我们该怎么办？​”我问。“我们该为自己搜刮能量，从任何可以找得到的地方。​”他回答。唐望解释说巫士有一套搜刮的方法，他们慧黠地重新分派他们的能量，去掉任何他们生命中虚浮的事物，他们称此为巫士的行径。基本上，唐望说巫士的行径是一连串应对这世界的行为选择，这些选择要比我们的社会所教导给我们的有智慧多了。这些巫士的选择是以改变我们对于生命的基本反应来重新整修我们的生命。
text.en: We can only have that much weight, and we use it all to be conscious and to deal with our food-eating world. He has repeatedly stressed that no more energy is available and that, because all the energy we can use is already available, there is nothing that can be used to make any unusual sense, such as dreaming. "What are we gonna do?" I asked. “We should search for our own energy from wherever we can find it. He answered. He explained that the witches had a way of scavenging, and that they had reassigned their energy and removed from their lives anything which they described as the deeds of witches. Basically, Tang would say that the acts of witches are a series of behavioural choices to deal with the world that are much more intelligent than our society teaches us. These witches have chosen to reshape our lives by changing our basic response to life.

A long dream, 2016
In the room where I was born, the blue floor tables...

text.zh:
昨夜梦到东村的老厝，在我出生的那间平房蓝色的瓷砖变得深不见底，我潜到下面发现好多从未见过的生物，像海底世界，到了海的最底层看见糖果一样大小的牛羊，和四只脚滑的很快像小鱼群一样的老鼠。陆面上的动物都缩小至少十倍的比例。当我一口气回到上面时，房间变成很多窗但是没有门的高楼，上面是一个荒芜的世界，空气干燥，除了人类还是人类，还有人造植被。突然一个女人晕倒在地上，然后出现两个穿白色衣服剃着寸头的年轻男子过来一边说她不能在这里领取免费的葡萄糖救济，一边将她拖走，走到窗边的时候他们不小心松了手那个女人从窗台那里掉了下去，我没有声音的尖叫了一下然后就开始哭，那两个人向我表示这是没办法的事情。     
Last night I dreamed of the old house in East Village. In the bungalow where I was born, the blue tiles had become a bottomless pool. I dove down and found myself in a strange underwater world, teeming with creatures I had never seen before. At the very deepest floor of the sea, there were cows and sheep the size of candy, and four‑legged rats that darted about like a shoal of fish. Every animal on land had shrunk to at least a tenth of its original size.
 
When I finally swam back up in one breath, the room had transformed into a towering building with countless windows but no doors. Above was a desolate world, its air dry and still, inhabited only by humans—humans and nothing else—save for artificial plants.
 
Then, a woman collapsed to the ground. Two young men in white, their hair cropped short, appeared and said she could not receive free glucose relief here. They dragged her toward the window, but as they reached it, their grip slipped. She fell from the windowsill.
 
I screamed without a sound, and then I cried. The two men looked at me and said there was nothing they could do.
text.en:
Last night I dreamt of an old school in East Village, and the blue tiles of the flat house I was born deep, and I went down to find a lot of creatures that I had never seen before, like the world of the sea floor, cattle and goats of the size of candy at the bottom of the sea, and four mice that slipped quickly like little fish. All the animals on the ground are reduced by at least 10 times. When I returned to the top, the room became a high-rise with windows but no doors, with a desolate world with dry air and artificial vegetation besides humans. Suddenly, a woman fainted, and then two young men dressed in white and shaved their heads came and said that she could not get free glucose relief here and dragged her away, and when they went to the window, they accidentally let the woman fall off the window, screaming without a voice, and started crying, and the two men told me that there was no way.
I dove down and found myself in a spiral world, seeing with rares I had never seen before.
 
When I finally swam back up in one break, the room had tried into a challenge building with country worlds but no doors.
 
Then, a woman fell to the ground.
 
The two men looked at me and said there was nothing they could do.

text.zh:
**雪崩**

很长很长的梦，一开始我们生活在小小的水塔里，很挤。夜晚，人们都来到街头，在广场点起火堆，我们看着，这火不知不觉蔓延。在马路边缘一个大火堆熊熊燃烧，远处还有好几个，火堆有两三米高，一边吐出灰烬，漫天扬尘。除了这火，所有一切都是灰色的。像揭阳冬至一样，尘土像雪一样洋洋洒洒的飘来，但梦里好像真的也在下雪。

我手里拿着塑料瓶，想扔在火堆里，不料它经过火堆被点燃后，又继续往马路上滚。这时候，一头庞大的驯鹿，一个成人站直伸直手臂可能连它的膝盖都摸不到，像幽灵公主里的山神，慢慢从画着白线的柏油马路上走过。我跑了几步但又停下，期待前面的人会把塑料瓶踢回火堆，但大家都看了一下，伸了一下手，没人去把它真的停止。这天杀的火瓶还在继续往前滚，滚到驯鹿的脚边，小小爆炸了，但这爆炸把马路边的大火堆引到了驯鹿身上，使它整个开始燃烧，驯鹿长啸一声，左倾，倒在地上，火在它身上蔓延之处，皮肤像腐烂一样变黑，变得干涸，然后突然浑身像游乐园降温水洒一样喷出鲜血，混入每一口人们吸入的空气，我们想逃，想止住呼吸，但没人能逃得掉。
text.en:
**Avalanche**

It's a long, long dream, and at first we're living in a small water tower, crowded. At night, people came to the streets and set fire to the square, and we watched as the fire spread. On the edge of the road, there is a large fire that burns, and several more are far away, two or three metres high, while the ashes are spitting out. Everything but this fire is gray. As the sun rises and winter rises, the dust floats like snow, but the dream seems to be snowing.

I had a plastic bottle in my hand and I tried to throw it in the fire, but it was lit by the fire, and then I went on to roll on the road. At this point, a large reindeer, with an adult standing straight up his arms, may not even be able to touch his knee, like the mountain god in the ghost princess, slowly passing through the white-lined tarp. I ran a few steps and stopped, hoping that the people in front would kick the plastic bottle back to the fire, but everyone looked at it, reached out and nobody really stopped it. The flaming flask continues to roll up to the feet of the reindeer, with a small explosion, but the explosion led the whole fire on the roadside to the reindeer, causing it to start burning, the reindeer to swung and left, to fall on the ground, and the fire spreads on it, its skin becomes black as decay, it drys out, and then suddenly spills blood like a warm water from the park, mixing it into the air that everyone breathes, and we want to flee, we want to stop breathing, but no one can escape.

山寨一词，在汉语里原先的意思是指筑有栅栏等防守工事的 山庄;

此后引申为贫穷之地，穷人的居住之处，以及旧时绿林好汉和强盗们占据的营寨，这个词汇也有着不被官方管辖的含义 （水浒传的基地就叫“山寨”）。

这些年，随着价格低廉和功能齐全的山寨手机流行之后，「山寨」 一词让「模仿」有了全新的含义，同时「模仿」原有的词义边界 也被取消，造假、侵权、不规范、开玩笑和恶作剧等等无需词义 的签证就可进入模仿的国度，成为山寨的臣民。可以这么说，山寨是今日汉语里最具有安那其主义精神的词汇。

## Pirate 海盗\盗版 简介

好像pirate对于我来说除了海贼王没什么关联，直到知道他也叫做盗版，想起我们看到的很多好东西都是pirate的。

在数字时代，“海盗”隐喻一方面被媒介公司和版权企业用作话语修辞，将盗版行为犯罪化以维护私人财产权利；另一方面，它也被欧洲和北美的行动者用作符号资源，与商业垄断权力抗争以倡导社会公共利益。

提到山寨理论，很多人都会想到韩炳哲写的《山寨-中国式解析》这本书。书中描述的中国，绝不是我们这一代人所经历的那个正在迅速现代化的中国。我想大多数受过现代教育的年轻人都对中国传统多少有些不屑。它们总是让我联想到那些互相吹捧的长辈。这本来也没什么好说的，直到我们看到了更加死气沉沉的当代艺术。
《山寨》的最后一章探讨了“山寨（假货/仿造）”本身。与前面提到的中国画不同，传统艺术虽然正在衰落，但至少是被认可的艺术。然而，“山寨”指代的却是那些从未被摆上台面的事物。我认为它甚至可以是一个人的“山寨”，比如为了谋生而进行的街头表演，我想就算是一瞬间的民俗也是民俗吧。
两年前我深圳的除夕夜遇到了这一幕。与传统中那些气势磅礴的舞狮队不同，这场单人舞狮在街头上似乎并不怎么受欢迎，他挨家挨户讨赏，我很想找出来分享给大家，但视频已经过期，只留下这张背影，我想我会永远记住他，从狮子嘴巴露出来的疲惫笑脸，动作中也流露出一种卑微的姿态，同时却又是整条街最勇敢的人。
这几年我山寨过纳西麒麟戏的木老师，摩梭东巴阿公塔，还有新正顺木偶剧团的团长李洁娜。总之我觉得和山寨对象相处，山寨思想品德课还蛮重要的。

text.zh:
最早是拜访了纳西吉祥村的麒麟戏。根据记载，这些面具本该在每次表演结束后被烧掉。然而，从80年代起，它们就没有再被烧掉然后重新制作（山寨）一次。非遗传承人木老师之所以不舍得烧掉它们，而是把自己的家变成了一个展览馆。 当我和朋友提出想要复刻这些面具时，木老师起初非常高兴。但几天后，当他发现我们山寨得有点离谱后，他就有些不太愿意教我们了。我想，这是因为麒麟舞目前正处于一个相当脆弱的境地。他希望能通过申请“非物质文化遗产”来保护它。“非遗”是一个非常现代的概念。它追求原创，而且如果不能促进旅游业，就不会被批准。所以我们只好离开了那个村子。
我还在云南摩梭村遇到一位东巴，阿公塔。那里没有美术馆，也没有旅游业，所以那位萨满相对来说更加自信。虽然他也不愿意教我（理由是他的手艺传男不传女），但当我在北京山寨了他的仪式发朋友圈后，阿老师还点赞了。所以我才会经常回到摩梭村找阿老师。
我之所以在潮汕学习木偶戏，除了学习这门艺术本身，更是为了更多地了解他们的生存方式。潮州的传统戏曲是少有的不依赖政府、旅游业或美术馆的艺术。它们是完全由民众支持的、自发且极其活跃的艺术形式。因此，那些民间艺人对我抱有非常开放的态度。

### MFA 聽上去有點洋氣有點高大上，就像 LV 一樣，你不複製粘貼都拼不出它的全名。山寨 MFA（Master of Fine Art, 山寨藝術碩士或山寨藝術大師）也差不多，就是些個草野小民搞得，不是正規的藝術，也不是專業的學校，那種是培養高級實用專門人才的，我們是假的，目的就是培養不高級、不實用、不專門的人。

IG：shanzhaiMFA。公眾號：山寨MFA，diyloveclub

通常每期時長一周到一月不等。每次都大不一樣，一期一會，一吟一詠，一言一行，一驚一乍。自二三年發起以來，在七個地方以不同主題和形態搞過十三次：

雲南大理（山寨藝術學校）

浙江台州（山寨幻想與妄想大會）

廈門大社（山寨家庭）

廈門翔安（山寨自然：瞎幾把玩泥巴大學）

杭州良渚（山寨奧林匹克運動會）

潮汕普寧（遊戲戲劇節和山寨潮汕）

泰國北部（三十一世紀原住民研究會）

上海（愛里斯恨*魔法學院）

廣東梅州（小妖精技校）

大理开源之家（宿舍祭）

潮汕揭阳（山寨潮剧团）

武汉（烂天使学校）

潮汕揭阳（东村戒美所）

- 作為臨時學校，它每次有至少兩位校友作為發起人，不搞申請、面試、篩選之類的，來了都是老師和同學，不斷互換，打掃衛生也可以是一堂課！支持搗亂，鼓勵逃課！包括發起者在內的所有人支付同樣的費用，不分老師學生，結束後根據合作社原則按勞動量再分配，發還給大家。
- 作為戲劇，不區分表演者和觀眾，不區分藝術家和公眾，不區分台上台下，通過分享服飾、場景、道具、樂器、遊戲、工作坊等等，展開隨時隨地的共同的即興創作。像劇團一樣，我們大部分人在寨中一起生活。在山寨的儀式、銳舞、行為、戲劇等現場中，你可以成為山寨演員、教授、藝術家、仙鶴、野生菌……做些山寨的美食、手工、行為藝術、寫作等。也可以被理解成社會實踐藝術，或者是臨時遊樂場，或者是交友會！

咱們這些個野路子，要是撿到點兒什麼機會啦，像什麼展覽、經費、對談會之類的。咱們得把那些光鮮亮麗的「資源」掰碎了、搗爛了，盡可能地往外撒，搞點兒分享啊、再分配啊，讓那些個平常沒啥這種機會的，也能分一杯羹！因為啊，那些不被看到的人，他們骨子裡頭那股子山寨的精氣神兒，可比咱們這些個自稱「山寨」的更濃烈！

不分裡外，打不死殺不完，真假難辨才是山寨。不想成為固定成員的類似藝術家組合或樂隊之類的，更想成為路邊兒那股子怪風，

風可沒有什麼品牌和IP！它就是那股子從泥巴地裡長出來的草根氣兒，是那種野得沒專業、糙得沒倫理、亂得沒責任、爛大街到毫無品質的範兒！

所以，MFA 啊有沒有都是次要的，反正都是冒牌貨。但那股子山寨魂兒，才是關鍵。山寨精靈就像個不認祖宗的孤魂野鬼，誰都能讓它附身，因為它在每個街角蓄勢待發：「來吧！讓我附體吧！用魔法打敗魔法！打假這個假冒偽劣的一切！一起把世界搞得雞飛狗跳！」

Most art projects begin—or end—with the question of how to do it. Yet more often than not, how to do it is really how to speak about it.

A Shanzhai Troupe is nor an art project. It is more ramshackle than the most ramshackle traveling band. It is more cheap than the cheapest art，It is not about what to do—sometimes it is about what not to do. Like the traditional Teochew Opera troupes:
1. The performance is not for the audience; in the middle of acting, they still pause to burn incense for the gods or ghosts.
2. They do not dine in restaurants; they carry their own stove.
3. They do not sleep in hotels; they bring their own beds.
4. They do not eat beef.

A Shanzhai Troupe can also simply be the practice of saying "No..."

中文版
受文者： 雲林縣政府文化觀光處
（或：雲林縣政府文化處／相關承辦單位）

主旨：
申請「AVIAMA 2026 Grants – Puppets and Mobility」計畫，懇請協助提供成員城市支持信（Letter of Support），敬請 惠允。

說明：

東村新婦山寨劇團受到潮州鐵支木偶戲啟發，以寺苗秀琴阿嬤留下的空蕩蕩的「床」為戲台，上演「東村」婦女們的故事——可以是任何一個普通村子裡一群會哭泣的強壯女人如何尋找生存門道的任何奇葩事。這是安放她們故事的一個與現實平行的地方。本人 Ye，目前為寶藏巖國際藝術村駐村藝術家，亦參與本團隊的創作與研究，並以此作為延伸行動的基礎。

東村新婦是一個開源漂流劇團，他們通過山寨劇團、不斷行走、公開招募、搭建臨時舞台的方式進行對話。東村新婦希望通過 AVIAMA 2026 GRANTS Puppets and Mobility 的支持，以潮汕東村為出發點，前往不同的城市學習、交流、表演。而雲林縣亦為 AVIAMA 成員城市，我們希望來到雲林縣進行交流學習，深入理解其深厚且持續發展中的布袋戲文化脈絡，觀察偶戲如何在地方社群之中被傳承、實踐，並於當代語境中不斷轉化與再生。

雲林縣長期作為臺灣布袋戲的重要發源與實踐場域，透過家族、師徒及地方社群之傳承系統，保存了豐富而立體的偶戲文化，並積極透過節慶、教育與國際交流，使偶戲文化得以持續被觀看、被理解與被討論。本團隊計畫於本次 AVIAMA 2026 Grants「Puppets and Mobility」申請中，將雲林縣作為重要之交流學習場域，實地觀摩與學習其創作實踐、傳承方式及地方文化脈絡。

本團隊期待於交流期間，透過觀摩、訪談與實際交流等方式，向雲林縣之偶戲工作者、團隊及文化實踐者學習，並分享東村新婦山寨劇團以行走、搭建臨時舞台及公開招募為核心之創作經驗，促進不同地區偶戲實踐之雙向交流與對話。我們亦希望透過公開招募的方式，在雲林縣招募劇團成員，並完成在雲林的演出，使交流不僅止於觀摩學習，更能實際落地為合作與共創。

本次前往雲林縣之交流學習，係本團隊申請 AVIAMA 2026 Grants 所規劃之國際移動與專業交流計畫之一環，期望藉此建立亞洲不同偶戲文化之實質連結，並將交流成果回饋於後續創作、分享及跨城市合作之中。文末另附本團隊相關創作與交流之公開連結，並附 AVIAMA 2026 Grants「Puppets and Mobility」公開徵件資訊連結，敬請參考。

基於上述計畫內容，謹此敬請 貴府作為 AVIAMA 成員城市，支持本團隊之交流學習計畫，並協助提供申請「AVIAMA 2026 Grants – Puppets and Mobility」所需之成員城市支持信（Letter of Support），以利本計畫順利推進。

如蒙 惠允，不勝感激。本團隊亦期待未來能與雲林縣於偶戲文化、藝術交流及國際合作等面向，建立持續且深入之交流關係。

** 备份
我们现在的主要山寨对象为新正顺木偶剧团，是一个活跃于潮汕的民俗老爷戏剧团，主要在潮汕地区为大小节日演酬神戏，历史上，潮州木偶戏原本为真人潮剧的翻版，在对其技艺和文化的记录的同时，我们对他们的生存方式更感兴趣，在舞台演绎背后，是剧团中每个人的情感连接、在共同度过的时光中找到自己在生活中的位置和生存的方式。我们跟随并向该木偶剧团学习潮剧技艺的同时，


东村新妇 云林演出计划书
项目介绍

- 背景
東村新婦山寨劇團受到潮州鐵支木偶戲啟發，以寺苗秀琴阿嬤留下的空蕩蕩的「床」為戲台，上演「東村」婦女們的故事——可以是任何一個普通村子裡一群會哭泣的強壯女人如何尋找生存門道的任何奇葩事。這是安放她們故事的一個與現實平行的地方。

我们现在的主要山寨对象为新正顺木偶剧团，是一个活跃于潮汕的民俗老爷戏剧团，主要在潮汕地区为大小节日演酬神戏，历史上，潮州木偶戏原本为真人潮剧的翻版，在对其技艺和文化的记录的同时，我们对他们的生存方式更感兴趣，在舞台演绎背后，是剧团中每个人的情感连接、在共同度过的时光中找到自己在生活中的位置和生存的方式。我们跟随并向该木偶剧团学习潮剧技艺的同时，也在学习他们的生存方式。因此，我们也想通过与当地的歌仔戏和掌中戏剧团合作的方式，交流潮剧偶戏演绎方法和各自的生存方式，

- 立场
缝纫微型经济与女性劳动可见化

### 核心立场

东村妇女因照护与家庭分工长期留守村内——喂奶、做饭、接送孩子、照顾老人。她们的日常劳动构成家庭运转的基础，却常常是"看不见"的工作。本项目从她们的经验出发，通过布偶与缝纫，让这些劳动与情感被看见、被讲述、被公平支付。


研究输出：把“山寨”整理为可传递的方法论与工具包，其中包括一个透明的微型流动经济模型模板。

在2025年1月的"缝纫开放周"试点中，萍姐、小玉等三位妇女操作缝纫机，每小时支付20元人民币，工作坊收入全部归她们所有。我们同时推出"一对一craft & talk"——参与者付费与东村妇女视频聊天，话题包括潮汕话、缝纫技术、婆媳关系、临终照护、死者托梦等，每小时20元或随喜。

时间线

* **阶段A（2026年4–5月）预备：**对接雲林伙伴与场地；伦理与授权流程；工具包与“床舞台”构件准备
* **阶段B（2026年5–6月）研学行走：**跟随“当地掌中戏或歌仔戏剧团”巡演；记录它们的生存原则
* **阶段C（2026年6月）雲林交流驻地（14天）：**观摩/访谈/实作工作坊；公开 work-in-progress + 讨论
* **阶段D（2026年7月）共同创作与演出：**沿途改写、制作、搭建临时舞台并演出；开放工作坊
* **阶段E（2026年9–12月）研究输出：**双语田野笔记 +《山寨剧团工具包》+ 影像日志/纪录片模块 + 系列分享讲座





《東村新婦山寨劇團——可移动“床戏台”与跨地域偶戏交流（台湾·雲林）》


東村新婦山寨劇團是一个开放式、漂流式的行动表演团体，灵感来自潮州铁枝木偶戏与潮剧等传统。项目从一种“缺席”开始：在东村生活了90年的祖母离世后，房间被清空，一个孩子问“老嬷去哪里了？”寺苗秀琴把老嫲留下的空床变成一个小小的偶戏舞台，并邀请东村的女性定期相聚、缝纫、共同创作“人形”偶，排练戏剧，把她们的故事安放在一个与现实平行的舞台空间中。东村妇女因照护分工长期困于村内、难以自由移动——她们的劳动支撑着家庭运转，却往往不被计入经济贡献。本项目将女性劳动可见化并公平支付，作为不可妥协的伦理底线。

对我们而言，“山寨”不是一种风格标签，而是一套工作方法：持续行走、公开招募、在不同地点搭建临时舞台，以此与当地发生对话。我们把创作过程进行开源：缝纫、音乐、操偶训练、排练与分享往往在公共场域进行，让每一站像庙会一样多重的维度进行交流。

我们现在的主要山寨对象为新正顺木偶剧团，是一个活跃于潮汕的民俗老爷戏剧团，主要在潮汕地区为大小节日演酬神戏，历史上，潮汕木偶戏原本为真人潮剧的精简版，通过不断的模仿技艺，是真正的草根文化，也是真正的山寨精神。

演绎背后，是剧团中每个人的情感连接、在共同度过的时光中找到自己在生活中的位置和生存的方式。我们除了跟随木偶剧团学习潮剧技艺之外，也在学习他们原住民的生活方式，在流动和融合中成为新的原住民。

我们希望本项目能为 AVIAMA 网络带来：在亚洲区域内更紧密的偶戏连接、以低技术/低成本的移动方式激发创作创新、以及可共享的专业文档与方法论输出。


我们希望在 AVIAMA 2026 “Puppets and Mobility” 的支持下，推进项目下一阶段，并把主要交流学习放在台湾雲林县——AVIAMA 成员城市，也是台湾布袋戏的重要重镇。我们计划以“观摩 + 访谈 + 实作交流”的形式，与当地偶戏工作者、制作师、文化实践者展开深入的专业交流，理解雲林布袋戏的传承体系、当代创作实践与地方社群之间的连接方式。

雲林驻地（10–14 天）拟开展的活动：

* 田野走访（场馆/剧团/典藏/节庆/庙会等，视当期资源而定）与访谈
* 技艺交流工作坊（操偶、制作、音乐/锣鼓与节奏整合等）
* 公开 work-in-progress 分享演出 + 座谈讨论（面向观众与专业人士）

预期产出

1. 一场面向公众的 work-in-progress 展示；
2. 一份英/法双语的田野笔记（方法、排练工具、伦理与工作流程）；
3. 一个可开源分享的“床戏台”山寨剧团工具包（基础结构方案 + 安全提示），供艺术家与 AVIAMA 网络参考与再利用。

2) 我们将把项目发展为三个互相关联的方向：

### 方向一：研学行走（Study Trip）——"一起生活，看同样的东西"

这不是旅游式参观，而是沉浸式共同生活与田野观察。我们已有与揭阳新正顺潮剧团共同生活的经验——搭台、演出、祭拜/酬神、用自带炉灶做饭、睡通铺。田野记录聚焦"原则与变通"：他们坚持什么（禁忌、戏令如军令、戏台上下的边界等），又如何在现实压力下变通。

关于为何做剧团，李洁娜团长曾回答："不是因为喜欢艺术，是因为做别的工作经常被欠钱，但谁都不敢欠潮剧团的钱。"——这正是我们希望深入理解的民间剧团生存智慧。
正如潮剧团长所说："这些戏是演给神看的。"

我们将刻意收集"非表演声音"——四小时演出后几乎没人在看，邻居做饭的声音，婴儿的哭声，施工的电焊声，观众的咳痰与交谈——把这些"噪音"视为表演生态不可分割的一部分。探索一种原住民符号是怎么形成的。

### 方向二：共同创作与演出（Production）——"边走边编，搭建临时现场"
* 关注潮州铁枝木偶与当代混合形式
参与制作的妇女们为布偶赋予了自己的分身：
- **陈小玉**（1994）的布偶"没有结婚，没有小孩，替我去外面看看世界"——她自己四个孩子的母亲，常年困于村内
- **可可**（1981）的布偶原本44岁，后来她说"高龄产妇不行，改成1998年比较好"
- **陈岐岐**（1984）的布偶"一开始是小丑，后来变成女巫"
- **理舟**（2000）的布偶"那孩子不一定是她生的，但她爱那个孩子"
- **小海**（1989）的布偶是"一滴海水，参与万物循环"
这些布偶携带着制作者的愿望、遗憾与幽默，成为她们移动受限人生的替身。女性不是被叙述的对象，而是通过偶成为叙述的主体与行动者。
我们以"多重身份"的工作方式运行：每个人同时是创作者与执行者（编剧兼厨师、敲击乐兼司机、控偶兼田野观察）。集体创作不代表去中性化，而是用“山寨”的流动方法
可以是符号的解构和重构、演出可以是抽象化的片段。重点是全过程：从无到有搭台，人群如何聚集、围观、互动，表演如何开始与结束——甚至"没有真正的开始与结尾"。

每一站都将配套开放工作坊，邀请当地人以任何形式加入（制作、表演、交谈）。我们已有"山寨潮剧团"的组织经验——2025年12月在潮汕组织七天七夜的学习行程，内容包括学缝纫、学潮剧、观看民俗活动与传统演出。

### 方向三：研究与方法论构建（Research）——"山寨作为一种流动方法" + 缝纫微型经济

我们将把实践过程理论化并工具化，形成可分享的"生存手册/工具包"。研究议题包括：
1.**"山寨"方法论**：我们如何通过对传统的"不完全临摹"与"创造性误读"生成自己的实践。我们关注"原则/变通"边界；

2. **临时公共空间**：临时舞台如何瞬间制造公共活动场域。萍姐说："无数次分开的路口，一个垃圾站点，它是东村的入口也是出口，只有孩子和老人会在这里寻宝。"

3. **多重身份与流动社群**：团队内部多角色协作，以及沿途吸纳临时成员（"原住民/临时加入者"）如何形成短暂而真实的流动社群；

4. **经济模型实验**：清晰区分交通/生活成本与表演创作收入，建立可持续、透明的微型流动经济。
---

Inquiry regarding AVIAMA 2026 Grants – Puppets and Mobility
Dear Sir or Madam,

My name is zhuyan ye. I am writing on behalf of Dongcun Xinfu Experimental Theatre, an independent experimental theatre collective initiated in the Chaoshan region of southern China. 

Dongcun Xinfu Experimental Theatre emerged from long-term engagement with local communities in Chaoshan. Inspired by Iron Rod Puppet, a traditional regional puppetry form, as well as local folk performance practices, our work focuses on women’s narratives, everyday labor, and strategies of survival embedded in local life. We often work with simple and mobile stage structures—such as beds, temporary platforms, and improvised sets—and develop performances through traveling, public open calls, community building, and site-specific performances.

Together with the collective, I am currently preparing an application for the AVIAMA 2026 Grants – Puppets and Mobility. As Bochum is a member city of AVIAMA, we are very interested in learning whether there may be relevant cultural departments, institutions, or contexts within the City of Bochum connected to puppetry, theatre, or international cultural exchange.

In 2025, I participated in a residency at ZK/U – Center for Art and Urbanistics in Berlin, where I further deepened my interest in German theatre and contemporary performance practices. Through the AVIAMA grant, Dongcun Xinfu Experimental Theatre hopes to engage in international exchange, to learn from local puppetry and performance contexts in different cities, and to contribute our experience of mobile, community-based theatre to cross-regional dialogue.

As part of the AVIAMA application process, a letter of support from an AVIAMA member city is required. We would therefore like to kindly inquire whether the City of Bochum might consider providing such a letter, and if so, what materials or information would be helpful for your consideration.

For your reference, links to our previous works, documentation, and related interviews are included below.

Thank you very much for your time and consideration.
I would sincerely appreciate any guidance you may be able to offer.

Yours faithfully,
zhuyan ye

East Village New Woman.
Project introduction

- Background
Toshimura's New Women's Village Theatre was inspired by the Thongzhou Iron Puppet, using the empty "bed" left by Tsing-Cheng, as a stage to play the story of the "East Village" women – anything strange about how a group of crying strong women in a common village could find their way to survival. It's a place where their stories are set in parallel to reality.

Our main target now is the Shino-Hung Puppet Theatre, an active folk drama group, which has been performing festivals and festivals, mainly in the Twig region. Historically, the Chouzhou puppet show was a replica of the real show. While we are more interested in their technical and cultural records, we are more interested in how they survive. Behind the stage is the emotional connection of everyone in the theatre, finding their place in life and how to survive in the time they spent together. We followed and studied the puppetatrical art as well as their ways of survival. So we also want to share the methods of the play and the way we live by working with the local operas and the troupes.

- Position.
Sewing microeconomics and female labour visibility

Core position

East Village women have long remained in the village - breastfeeding, cooking, delivering children and caring for the elderly - because of the division of care and family responsibilities. Their day-to-day work forms the basis for the functioning of the family, but is often an "unseen" job. The project is based on their experience, through puppets and sewing, so that the work and emotions are seen, told and fairly paid.


Research output: Collapse the “shelter” into a tradable methodology and toolkit, including a transparent template for micro-mobile economy models.

In January 2025, three women, Ping and Yu, operated sewing machines, paid 20 yuan per hour, and earned all the income in the workshop. At the same time, we have introduced "one-on-one craft & talk" - participants pay to chat video with East Village women on such topics as hip-hop, sewing techniques, in-laws, end-of-life care, dreams of the deceased, etc., at $20 per hour or with pleasure.

Timeline

:: **Preparation for Phase A (April-May 2026): **Computers and sites; ethics and authorization processes; toolkits and “bed stage” components
:: ** Phase B (May-June 2026) research walk: ** Following the tour of the Local Hand-in-hand or Opera Group; document their survival principles
:: ** Phase C (June 2026) Cloud forest exchange site (14 days):** observation/interview/workshop; open work-in-process + discussion
:: ** Phase D (July 2026) co-creation and performance:** rewriting, making, setting up and performing a temporary stage along the way; open workshops
:: ** Phase E (September-December 2026) research output: ** Bilingual field notebooks + Kits of the Shan troupe + Image log/documentary module + Series Sharing Lectures





The East Village New Women's Circus - Mobile Bed Table and Trans-Taiwan Polling


The East Village New Women's Village Theatre is an open, drifting group of operational performances inspired by traditions such as the Twidden State Iron Puppet and the Tide Theatre. The project began with an “absent”: after 90 years of living in Toshimura, the room was emptied and a child asked, “Where is Grandma?” It turns the empty beds left behind by the old man into a small dove stage and invites the women of the East Village to meet regularly, to sewing, to co-create “human” dolls, to rehearse the theatre and to place their stories in a stage space parallel to reality. Women in the East Village have long been trapped in the village by the division of care and are unable to move freely - their work supports the functioning of the family but is often not factored into economic contributions. This project has made female labour visible and fairly paid as an irreconcilable ethical base.

For us, the fortress is not a style label, but a set of working methods: continuous walking, open recruitment, and the setting up of temporary arenas in different locations to engage in dialogue with the locals. We open up the creation process: sewing, music, puppet training, rehearsal and sharing, often in the public domain, so that each station can communicate as many dimensions as a temple.

Our main target now is the Shino-Hung Puppets, an active folk drama group, which has been performing fairs for festivals and festivals, mainly in the twilight regions. Historically, the twilight puppets were a simple version of the reality show, a true grass-roots culture and a true spirit through continuous imitation.

Behind the show is the emotional connection of everyone in the theatre, finding their place in life and the way they survive in the time they spend together. In addition to following the puppet theatre, we are also learning about their Aboriginal way of life and becoming new Aboriginals in mobility and integration.

We hope that this project will bring to the AVIAMA network a closer interlude in Asia, a low-technology/low-cost move to stimulate creative innovation, and a shared professional document and methodological output.


We hope to move forward with the next phase of the project, with the support of AVIAMA 2026 “Puppets and Mobility”, and to place the main exchange of learning in the city of the member of the AVIAMA county of Taiwan, which is also an important town for Taiwan’s bagplay. We plan to engage in in-depth professional exchanges with local doll workers, producers and cultural practitioners, in the form of "watching + interviewing + real-life exchanges" to understand the transmission systems of the cloud-covered play, contemporary creative practices and local communities.

Activities to be carried out by the cloud site (10-14 days):

:: Field visits (theatrical/theatre/distribution/festivities, etc., depending on current resources) and interviews
:: Technical exchange workshops (prostitution, production, music/drum and rhythm integration, etc.)
* Open work-in-procress shared performance + discussion sessions (for viewers and professionals)

Expected outputs

1. A work-in-process exhibition for the public;
2. An English/French bilingual field notebook (methodology, rehearsal tools, ethics and workflow);
An open-source shared tool kit (Infrastructure Program + Security Alert) for artists and the AVIAMA network for reference and reuse.

2) We will develop the project into three interrelated directions:

Direction one: Study Trip -- "Live together, watch the same thing."

This is not a tourist visit, but an immersion of living together and field observation. We already have the experience of living with the Shinoyang Shincheng troupe — setting up stage, performing, worshiping/rewarding, cooking with our own stoves and sleeping. Field records focus on "principles and variations": what they insist on (rejection, charades such as military orders, boundaries up and down the stage, etc.) and how they adapt under real pressure.

With regard to the reason for being a troupe, Commander Li Jenna said, "Not because he likes art, but because he is often owed money for other jobs, but no one dares to owe the troupe. " — That is the wisdom of the folk theatre that we want to understand in depth.
As the head of the tide shows, "These plays are for God."

We will deliberately collect "non-acting voices" — almost no one is watching after four hours of performance, the voices of neighbours cooking, the crying of babies, the electric welding of construction, the coughing and talking of viewers — these noises are seen as an integral part of the performance ecology. To explore how an indigenous symbol is formed.

# Direction 2: Co-production and performance #
:: Focus on contemporary mixed forms of Twilight Puppets
The women who participated in the production gave their parts to the puppets:
- ** Chen Xiaoyu** (1994) "No marriage, no children, go see the world for me" Her mother, four of her children, was trapped in the village. Internal
- ** Coco** (1981)'s doll was 44 years old, and then she said, "No, no, no, no.
- ** Chen Shui** (1984) "First clown, then witch."
- ** canoe** (2000)'s puppet: "She doesn't have the baby, but she loves the baby."
- ** Little Sea** (1989) is "A drop of sea water, participating in the cycle of everything."
These puppets carry the wishes, regrets and humor of the producers and become their replacement for moving their limited lives. Women are not the subject of a description, but are sometimes the subjects and actors of the narrative.
We operate in a "multi-identity" working style: each person is the creator and the implementer at the same time. Collective creation does not mean neutralization, but rather a mobile way of "shelter."
It can be deconstructing and reshaping symbols, and performances can be abstracted. The focus is on the whole process: from nothing to nothing, how the crowds gather, look, interact, how the performance begins and ends — and even “there is no real beginning and end”.

Each station will be accompanied by an open workshop in which locals will be invited to participate in any form (production, performance, talk). We already have the experience of organizing the "Campaign Tide" — a seven-day, seven-night study tour organized in December 2025 at the tide, which included sewing, study of the tide, and watching folk events and traditional performances.

# # Direction Three: Research and Methodology Construction #

We will theoretically and tool the practice into a shared "survival manual/tool kit". Research topics include:
1.** "Standing" methodological theory**: How do we generate our own practice through a "less than complete reading of tradition" and "creative misreading". We are concerned with the "principle/alternative" boundary;

2. **Temporary public space**: how the temporary stage creates an instant public sphere of activity. Ping said, "Many times at separate intersections, a dump, it's an entrance to East Village and an exit, where only children and the elderly will find treasure."

3. ** Multi-identity and mobile communities**: multi-role collaboration within the team and how to bring in temporary members along the way ( "Aboriginals/Temporary Joiners") to form short and real mobile communities;

4. **The economic model experiment**: a clear distinction between transport/living costs and income from performance creation and a sustainable and transparent micro-mobile economy.

Dongcun Xinfu Experimental Theatre x Yunlin Exchange
---Chaoshan Puppetry Theatre Culture Exchange and Research Project 
AVIAMA 2026 Grants – Puppets and Mobility Application

一、东村新妇介绍

東村新婦實驗劇團是一個開放式、漂流式的行動表演團體，發起於中國揭阳的东村，長期以地方生活、女性經驗與傳統表演形式的當代轉化為核心關注。劇團受到潮州鐵支木偶戲（Iron Rod Puppet）、潮劇與民間儀式表演啟發，尤其以活跃在揭阳的新正顺木偶剧团为方法参照——历史上，潮汕木偶戏本就源自对真人潮剧的模仿与精简，并在流动巡演中形成自身文化。因此，我们延续此种“在模仿中生成”的路径，将东村女性苗子的祖母过世后留下的空床作为戏台，把它转变成簡易、可移動的舞台結構，發展出一種與現實平行的敘事空間，用以承載村莊女性的生命故事與日常勞動。

二、剧团运转方法

延续潮剧团的实践，「山寨」是我们的工作方法：透過持續行走、公開招募、臨時搭建舞台與在地合作，讓創作在不同地點與社群中生成--------搭台、演出、用自带炉灶做饭、睡通铺，而剧团成员的身份也是多重的，控偶师兼木工、乐手兼司机、写作者兼厨师...与这样的表演实践平行运转的，是我们维持生存的“漂流经济模型”。每至一地，我们便通过在地工作坊、手工艺品销售及演出，建立即时的收入循环。模型以透明的成本收益分割为基础，确保所有参与女性的劳动被看见，并直接获得经济回报。

二、Yunlin Exchange計畫目標

雲林縣長期為臺灣布袋戲重鎮，並為 AVIAMA 國際偶戲聯盟之成員城市，具有深厚的潮剧木偶戲文化基礎與當代推廣經驗。東村新婦實驗劇團希望透過本次交流計畫，向雲林縣學習布袋戲技藝、制度與生存模式，同時分享自身在移動式劇場、社群導向創作與跨文化實踐方面的經驗，建立亞洲區域內更緊密的偶戲交流關係。

本项目计划于2026年展开，形成一个从准备、研学到创作与知识回馈的完整闭环。我们将首先完成与云林县的对接及移动戏台的筹备，随后跟随新正顺潮剧团进行巡演与田野研学。以此为基础，团队将在云林县进行为期10-14天的深度驻地，走访当地布袋戏与歌仔戏剧团，举办工作坊，并最终以一场公开的“work-in-progress”偶戏展示与讨论作结。档案成果将汇聚通过田野笔记和漂流实践，整理为《山寨剧团工具包手册》以及影像日志和短纪录片模块。

Dongcun Xinfu Experimental Theatre x Yunlin Exchange
---Chaoshan Puppetry Theatre Culture Exchange and Research Project 
AVIAMA 2026 Grants – Puppets and Mobility Application

1.Introduction to Dongcun Xinfu Experimental Theatre

The Dongcun Xinfu Experimental Theatre is an open, itinerant performance collective originating from Dongcun Village in Jieyang, China. Our work centers on the lives of women in county towns and transforms traditional performance forms as a medium for their expressions. Drawing inspiration from Iron Rod Puppetry originated in Chaoshan Region, folk rituals, and the working methods of the Jieyang-based Xinzhengshun Puppet Troupe, we extend the historical logic of how Teochew puppet theatre itself originated as a condensed imitation of live opera. Following this path of “producing through imitating,” we made the empty bed left by Miaozi’s grandmother in Dongcun into a initimate, portable puppetry theater. It became a narrative space parallel to reality, carrying lived experiences of the village women.

2.Operation Method of Dongcun Xinfu Experimental Theatre

Building on the survival wisdom of traditional Chaoshan opera troupes, “Shanzhai” is our core methodology. We produce performances within different locations and communities through continuous travel, open recruitment, temporary stage-building, and local collaboration. Members of the troupe also hold multiple roles, such as puppeteer-carpenter, musician-driver, and writer-cook. Operating in parallel with this artistic practice is our essential "Drifting Economic Model." In each location, we establish an immediate and transparent cycle of income through local workshops, handicraft sales, and performances. The model is based on a clear division between costs and revenues, ensuring that the labor of all participating women is made visible and directly compensated, allowing creative work and livelihood to sustain each other in a state of constant movement.

3.Yunlin Exchange Project Goal

Yunlin County is a major hub for Taiwanese glove puppetry (Budaixi) and a member city of AVIAMA. It possesses a profound foundation in traditional puppetry culture and extensive experience in fostering contemporary practice. Through this exchange project, the Dongcun Xinfu Experimental Theatre hopes to learn from local puppetry groups in Yunlin: their theatrical techniques and organizational systems, while also sharing our experiences in vernacular puppetry performances, drifting theater and "shanzhai" methodology. Our aim is to foster diaglogues for the diverse puppetry practices within the Asian region.

Scheduled for 2026, this project will unfold as a complete cycle—from preparation and immersive research to collaborative making and sharing. We will begin by finalizing partnerships in Yunlin County and preparing our trip. This will be followed by a period of field study, traveling alongside the Xinzhengshun Chaoshan Opera Troupe to learn from their touring practice.

Building on this foundation, the team will undertake a 10–14 day intensive residency in Yunlin. This core phase will include visits to local glove puppet (Budaixi) and Gezai opera troupes. We will culminate the residency in a open puppet theatre performance and hosting open-discussion.

All documentation from field notes and our drifting practice will be synthesized into our key archive: the Shanzhai Theatre Toolkit handbook, accompanied by a video log and a short documentary module.
